# Intake Brief: Assert at the unit's observable contract — calibration for `toHaveBeenCalledWith`

**Work Item:** SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G
**Issue Type:** task
**Priority:** medium

## Problem statement

The suite has no recorded rule for when a call-argument assertion (`toHaveBeenCalledWith`, `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith`, `mock.assert_called_once_with`, `mock.call_args_list`) is legitimate and when it pins private wiring, so reviewers and agents judge each occurrence ad hoc. The churn analysis that raised this item (WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ) assumed call-argument assertions on internal collaborators were an unalloyed cost; the follow-up migration (WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM) falsified that: of 155 occurrences in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts`, **148 were retained** as genuine boundary/observable-contract assertions and only **7 were migrated** to outcome assertions. The gap is therefore not "assert less on calls" but "record the retain/migrate rule, require each retained assertion to name the contract it observes, and flag the narrow remainder automatically".

## Users

- **Test author / AI agent** writing a new test — needs a decidable rule for whether to assert a call, and what to assert instead.
  - *User story:* "As an agent writing a downtime test, I want to know whether asserting `spawnFn` was called is legitimate, so I neither delete a genuine boundary assertion nor add a private-wiring one."
- **Reviewer / auditor** — needs a checklist item plus a justification convention so the judgement is auditable rather than a matter of taste.
  - *User story:* "As a reviewer, I want every retained call assertion to carry a one-line `Observable contract:` justification, so I can tell a boundary assertion from pinned wiring without reading the production code."
- **Test-suite maintainer** — wants one canonical rule referenced by the implement, test, triage and test-churn skills, so pruning and remediation decisions agree.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Anti-pattern entry added (calibration, not a blanket ban).** `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` gains an anti-pattern entry covering call-argument assertions on internal collaborators (`toHaveBeenCalledWith`, `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith`, and the Python analogues `mock.assert_called_once_with` / `mock.call_args_list`), with rationale, a positive alternative, and a matching bullet in the "Positive Guidance" list. The entry must state the **retain/migrate decision rule** rather than "prefer behaviour assertions over call assertions": the item's original headline is contradicted by the 148-retain/7-migrate evidence.
2. **Retain/migrate rule recorded verbatim from the approved precedent.** The entry adopts the rule producer-approved for WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM (plan Q1 = A) and cites it: **retain** calls on injected `deps` / boundary adapters (`spawnAgentPane`, `claimItem`, `closePane`, `spawnFn`, anchor/reaper lookups), observable output streams (`stderrSpy`, `stderr`/`stdout` capture), injected callbacks that are the sole observable channel (`fetcher`, `onProxyIdle`), and `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` ordering assertions *unless* an outcome assertion already proves the same ordering; **migrate** listener-shape wiring (`handle.once('error'|'exit', …)`, `addEventListener(…)`) where the same test drives the listener and asserts the resulting outcome, and redundant query-call assertions whose behaviour is already proven by a returned outcome or state. Each retained assertion must carry a one-line `Observable contract: …` justification naming *why* that boundary is observable.
3. **Concrete before/after example from the shipped migration.** The entry quotes the real pair from commit `f37c74ce` (WL-0MV98A2S2000USLX): the removed `expect(handle.once).toHaveBeenCalledWith('error', expect.any(Function))` / `('exit', …)` wiring assertions in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts`, replaced by the outcome assertion already present in the same test (`expect(spawned).toEqual({ ok: false, error: 'ENOENT: send-to-pi.sh' })`); plus one **retained** case with its justification comment (`spawnFn` boundary adapter in the same file; `markNeedsProducerReview` at `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts:846`).
4. **Review workflows reference the entry so it is actually applied.** `skill/test/SKILL.md` (§ 3 anti-pattern list), `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (test-writing step), `skill/triage/SKILL.md` (anti-pattern cross-reference) and `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` (pruning checklist) each name the new entry; no other workflow duplicates the rule's text.
5. **Advisory detector added.** `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` gains a detector that flags only the narrow migrate-shaped signatures: call-argument assertions on listener-shape mocks (`handle.once(…)`, `.on(…)`, `addEventListener(…)`) and call assertions duplicated by an outcome assertion in the same test. It contributes a `VETO`-style reason and can only ever produce `report-to-user` (never `remove`), consistent with the file's conservative verdict policy. Boundary-adapter assertions (`spawnFn`, `claimItem`, `deps.*`, `stderrSpy`) must not be flagged.
6. **Detector tests added.** `tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py` gains unit tests for the detector: a positive case (listener-shape wiring), a positive case (assertion duplicated by an outcome assertion), and a negative case proving a boundary-adapter assertion is not flagged even when it uses `toHaveBeenCalledWith`.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (e.g. `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` where the pruning checklist is described).
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Guidance + advisory detection only — **no refactoring of existing tests in this item**. Re-litigating the 148 retained herdr assertions is out of scope.
- Extend `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`; do not create a new document.
- The new entry must not weaken existing anti-patterns and must not read as licence to delete boundary assertions.
- The detector must be advisory only: it can never cause `remove`, and it must not gate the suite (no non-zero exit, no lint failure).
- Cross-repo citations are acceptable as evidence — existing entries already cite Tableau-Card-Engine paths — so quoting ContextHub `packages/herdr` files and `WL-…` items is in bounds.
- UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — 8 anti-patterns + 8 positive-guidance bullets; **no** entry for call-argument assertions (`grep -rn toHaveBeenCalled skill/ command/` returns nothing).
- Referenced today by `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `skill/triage/SKILL.md`, `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md`, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` — regex, language-agnostic (`_WEAK_ASSERT_RE` already matches `toBeDefined`/`toBeTruthy`, so JS/TS files are in scope); verdicts are `keep` / `remove` / `report-to-user`, with `report-to-user` the fallback for uncertainty. Tests live in `tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py`.
- ContextHub `packages/herdr`: 369 `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences across `*.test.ts*` (top files `index.test.ts` 41, `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` 36, `worklist.test.ts` 35, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` 30). `downtime-worker.test.ts` is now 2,245 lines / 24 occurrences after the split (WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX) — the "13,103 lines / 679 `vi.fn()`" figure in the original background predates that split.
- This repo's own Python suite: 13 `assert_called_once_with` and 99 `call_args_list` uses (e.g. `skill/implement/tests/test_risk_effort_gate.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`) — governed by the same rule under AC1.

## Desired change

One new calibration entry in the shared test-writing guidelines (retain/migrate rule + `Observable contract:` justification convention, both JS/TS and Python idioms, two real examples), referenced from the four consuming skill workflows, plus a narrow advisory detector with positive and negative unit tests. Net effect: call-assertion legitimacy becomes decidable from a written, cited rule; retained assertions become auditable; the small genuinely-wiring subset is flagged automatically without risking the legitimate boundary majority.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — new anti-pattern entry ("Call-argument assertions on internal wiring") + matching Positive Guidance bullet.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` — new `_detect_*` function + `VETO` reason (advisory, `report-to-user` only).
- `tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py` — detector unit tests (listener-shape positive, duplicate-of-outcome positive, boundary-adapter negative).
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — add the entry to the § 3 anti-pattern list.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — reference the new entry in the test-writing step.
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — anti-pattern cross-reference.
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — add the entry to the pruning checklist (step 2).
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — mention the new anti-pattern where the checklist is described.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** the item belongs in SorraAgents because `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` and the skills are canonical here; ContextHub consumes them through the global skill install and supplies the example test files.
- **Assumption:** the ContextHub producer-approved rule (WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM Q1 = A) is encoded verbatim, so the canonical guideline and the shipped precedent cannot diverge (producer answer Q3 = A).
- **Assumption:** the detector's "duplicated by an outcome assertion in the same test" test is a same-test heuristic (an outcome assertion — `expect(spawned)`, `expect(outcome)`, `expect(result)` — present in the same `it`/`test` body), not a global cross-file analysis (producer answer Q1 = B).
- **Risk — misleading headline:** shipping "prefer behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith`" as written would license deleting boundary assertions that carry real defect detection (7/155 evidence). Mitigation: AC1's calibration phrasing, AC2's verbatim rule.
- **Risk — false-positive automation:** a detector firing on legitimate boundary assertions erodes trust in `evaluate_usefulness.py` and could prompt unjustified deletions downstream. Mitigation: narrow listener-shape signature, `report-to-user` ceiling, explicit negative test (AC6).
- **Risk — justification-comment rot:** `// Observable contract:` comments can become copy-paste boilerplate. Mitigation: the entry requires naming *what the caller can observe*, not merely the comment's presence.
- **Risk — scope creep:** a broader mock-density budget, a herdr-wide assertion refactor, or an ESLint rule for ContextHub would follow naturally from this. Record as linked work items, do not consume here.
- **Risk — doc drift:** four skills reference the same list; changing the list in one place only would leave reviewers applying a stale checklist. Mitigation: AC4 enumerates all four.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ** (ContextHub) — test-churn/rewrite analysis; the evidencing analysis cited in this item's original background.
- **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** (ContextHub, completed) — split `downtime-worker.test.ts` into 14 focused files; its AC4 ("prefer observable outcomes over `toHaveBeenCalledWith`") was deferred to the item below.
- **WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM** (ContextHub, completed) — migrate `toHaveBeenCalledWith` → observable outcomes; holds the producer-approved retain/migrate rule this item encodes. Children: WL-0MV989W3U008ZYXN (F1 classification, comment `WL-C0MVBQJLJH004BZPE`, 148 retain / 7 migrate), WL-0MV98A00C0039A3E (F2), WL-0MV98A2S2000USLX (F3 migration, commit `f37c74ce`), WL-0MV98A5X3006WKQ0 (F4 verification).
- **WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL** (ContextHub, completed) — downtime worker test suite (source of the example files).
- **SA-0MSAC1IAS007I3K8** — follow-up wiring `evaluate_usefulness.py` into all code-touching skills; the detector added here must respect that wiring rather than duplicate it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — Automated detection scope (AC5)

**Question:** Should this item add automated detection, or stay guidance-only?

- **A.** Guidance + review checklists only; reword AC5 to put automated detection explicitly out of scope.
- **B.** Guidance + an advisory (`report-to-user`, never auto-remove) detector in `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`, narrowly keyed to listener-shape wiring (`handle.once(…)`, `addEventListener(…)`) and to call assertions already duplicated by an outcome assertion in the same test, with unit tests.
- **C.** Guidance + a custom ESLint rule in ContextHub `packages/herdr` (cross-repo; separate work item).
- **Recommended:** B — delivers AC5 with a decidable, testable signature while staying advisory; A is the smallest option; C leaves the canonical guidance repo behind.

**Answer (producer, 2026-10-28, interactive reply): B.** Implemented as AC5 + AC6.

### Q2 — Language scope of the entry

**Question:** Should the entry cover only JS/TS/Vitest idioms, or also the Python analogues used by this repo's own suite?

- **A.** Both — language-neutral framing, one JS/TS idiom (`toHaveBeenCalledWith`) and one Python idiom (`mock.assert_called_once_with` / `call_args_list`) example.
- **B.** JS/TS only — matches the evidence base, keeps the entry short.
- **Recommended:** A — the guideline is global and this repo's own suite has 13 `assert_called_once_with` and 99 `call_args_list` uses that the rule should govern.

**Answer (producer, 2026-10-28, interactive reply): A.** Implemented as AC1's explicit Python-idiom coverage.

### Q3 — Source of the retain/migrate rule

**Question:** Should the entry adopt the existing producer-approved ContextHub rule verbatim, or restate the rule independently?

- **A.** Adopt the rule approved for WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM (plan Q1 = A) and cite it as the source, so guideline and shipped precedent cannot diverge.
- **B.** Restate the rule in the guideline's own words from first principles and cite ContextHub as corroborating evidence only.
- **Recommended:** A — the rule is already producer-approved and empirically calibrated (148 retain / 7 migrate); a second, differently-worded rule would recreate exactly the ambiguity this item exists to remove.

**Answer (producer, 2026-10-28, interactive reply): A.** Implemented as AC2's verbatim adoption + citation.

### Research notes (answered by repo/worklog inspection, not by the producer)

- **Q: Is the "13,103 lines / 837 tests / 679 `vi.fn()`" figure in the background still accurate?** — No. `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` is 2,245 lines with 24 `toHaveBeenCalledWith` and 73 `vi.fn()` after WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX split it into 14 focused files. Source: `wc -l` + grep, 2026-10-28.
- **Q: Does the guideline file already mention call-argument assertions?** — No; `grep -rn toHaveBeenCalled skill/ command/` returns nothing. Source: repo grep.
- **Q: Where is automated detection possible today?** — `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` (regex, language-agnostic, already matches JS/TS assertions) and the `skill/refactor` smell detector; the former has an existing test module (`tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py`) to extend. Source: inspection of both scripts and the test module.
- **Q: Was the "call-argument assertions on internal collaborators" cost assumption validated?** — No. The ContextHub migration retained 148 of 155 occurrences as legitimate boundary assertions; only 7 were wiring (4 `handle.once`, 3 redundant tier queries). # Run mutation testing on top-churn modules to measure real test value

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measures how test code evolves (rewrite ratio, growth, stability), but not whether those tests **detect faults**. The largest suites are also the most mock-heavy, so a high line count and long survival could reflect tests that exercise mocks rather than behaviour. Until we measure fault detection directly, conclusions about TDD return on investment rest on a proxy. Mutation testing injects small faults into source code and checks whether the suite fails; the mutation score turns "big suite" into "does this suite earn its runtime".

## Users

- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants per-module mutation scores to validate or falsify TDD-ROI claims.
- **Maintainer of the agent infrastructure** — wants a pinned, reproducible campaign that can be rerun and compared over time.
- **Agent implementing testing-policy work** — wants one documented command and machine-readable output.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want a mutation-score table for the top-churn suites so I can see whether their size reflects real fault detection.
- As the infrastructure maintainer, I want the tool pinned and the command documented so a rerun is comparable.
- As an agent, I want the results in JSON so the test-value aggregator can consume them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A mutation-testing tool is selected and documented — **Stryker Mutator with the vitest runner** is the working choice — with rationale, licence (Apache-2.0) and version pinned in a lockfile.
- [ ] AC2: The campaign runs against the **source modules primarily exercised by the top three churn test suites**, with a documented suite→source mapping, and reports a mutation score per module and overall.
- [ ] AC3: Results are joined with each suite's size and mock density, and the hypothesis ("high-volume, mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults") is explicitly tested rather than asserted.
- [ ] AC4: Findings are written up and appended to the TDD-value assessment with explicit caveats: sampling/scoping, equivalent mutants, mutants killed for brittle internal-coupling reasons, and runtime cost.
- [ ] AC5: The campaign is reproducible — pinned tool version, documented command, deterministic config, and automated tests for the wrapper/report parsing — and does not regress the target project's test suite.
- [ ] AC6: Runtime cost is measured and bounded (confirmed bound: ≤15 min per module, ≤45 min per scoped run, weekly or per-release) so the campaign can be run periodically; the bound and cadence are documented. If the campaign **cannot produce results within the bound**, the report must flag this explicitly rather than silently returning partial/no results. The periodic run is scheduled on a **per-project day/time that spreads CPU load** across projects.
- [ ] AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the target repository; no source changes to the analysed project.
- Scoped mutation, not whole-repo: `worklist.ts` is 5,944 lines and must be limited to functions its tests actually exercise.
- Mutation tooling is not part of the target project's normal CI test suite (runtime cost).
- Periodic runs must be scheduled per project on a day/time chosen to spread CPU load (no two campaigns contending for the same host slots).
- A run that cannot complete within the bound must fail loudly (flagged as a budget breach with the partial result), never silently degrade to no result.
- No hardcoded project paths; the target root is an argument and is resolved like `skill/test-churn`.
- Equivalent mutants and sampling are documented limitations, not silently ignored.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is owned by the ship release pipeline and is not hand-edited here.
- Follow the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn` already produces the top-churn input. Analysis of `ContextHub` ranks these test files highest: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (101 commits), `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (84), `tests/database.test.ts` (72).
- Source mapping verified by imports:
  - `downtime-worker.test.ts` → `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (239 lines).
  - `worklist.test.ts` → `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (5,944 lines).
  - `database.test.ts` → `src/database.ts` (93-line re-export wrapper) plus the real implementation `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (2,083 lines).
- `ContextHub` uses `vitest`; neither it nor SorraAgents has Stryker installed today.
- Static anti-pattern detection exists in `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` plus `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`; it is a cheap pre-filter, not behavioural evidence.
- Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` names mutation testing as its evidence/tie-break arm.

## Desired change

- Add `skill/mutation-test/` with a pinned Stryker config, a wrapper that resolves the target root, scopes mutation, invokes Stryker and parses its JSON report, and tests for both.
- Run the campaign against the `ContextHub` top-three modules and record per-module scores, mutant counts and runtime.
- Join the scores with churn size and mock density and write the interpretation, including the explicit hypothesis verdict and caveats.
- Document the periodic command, the runtime bound and the scoping rules.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/mutation-test/SKILL.md` — Skill contract: purpose, when-to-use, workflow, outputs, limitations.
- `skill/mutation-test/stryker.conf.json` — Pinned Stryker/vitest-runner config and mutation scope.

## Related work

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** broader runtime budgets, more modules, or other languages must be filed as linked work items, not pulled into this item.
- **Runtime risk:** `worklist.ts` is very large; without function-level scoping the campaign will exceed any reasonable budget. Scoping rules are part of the deliverable.
- **Equivalent-mutant risk:** some survivors cannot be killed. The report must caveat this and sample-review survivors rather than treating every survivor as weak coverage.
- **Brittle-kill risk:** a mutant can be killed because a test asserts an internal collaborator call, not observable behaviour. Record this separately using the assertion-quality signal.
- **Confirmed (producer, 2026-11-01) — Q1:** the campaign lives in a reusable `skill/mutation-test/` in SorraAgents, not a ContextHub-local script, because AC5 requires a pinned reproducible command and SorraAgents is the canonical skills home.

If results are not obtained within that budget, flag it clearly (budget breach + partial result) rather than reporting nothing; schedule the run on a per-project day/time that spreads CPU load.

# Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects

## Problem statement

The `test-churn` / TDD-value analysis skill only runs when an agent remembers to
invoke it, so test-suite growth and rewrite trends across the managed projects
are not monitored continuously. The herdr downtime dispatcher already runs
per-project scheduled prompts (`/skill:refactor`, `/skill:standup`) from
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, but `test-churn` is not registered anywhere,
so no project produces periodic test-health evidence.

## Users

- **Maintainer / producer** — "I want weekly test-churn evidence for every
  managed project without asking an agent to run it."
- **Agent starting refactor or planning work** — "I want the latest test-health
  report to already exist when I start, so I can spot a suite growing without
  benefit."
- **Dispatcher operator** — "I want the schedule to fail closed, be visible
  when a project cannot be analysed, and never block the host with simultaneous
  heavy scans, so a stale or missing report never looks healthy."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `/skill:test-churn` entry is registered in SorraAgents'
   `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` using the existing schema (`id`, non-empty
   `prompt`, positive `intervalDays`, valid `HH:MM` `time`, and
   `lastTriggeredAt`), with the first provision setting a deterministic,
   staggered `lastTriggeredAt` seed and a distinct `time` (see AC3);
   re-running provisioning neither duplicates the entry, re-staggers it, nor
   changes any other entry's `lastTriggeredAt`.
2. Every configured managed project root receives the same entry via
   create-if-absent provisioning of its own
   `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`; this explicitly includes
   **Tableau-Card-Engine**, which currently has no scheduled-prompts file, so
   the command must create one. Absent or non-existent roots are skipped with a
   logged warning; the provisioning command supports `--dry-run` and is
   idempotent (a second run reports "already present" and writes nothing).
3. **Staggering (no CPU blocking):** provisioned entries are spread
   deterministically across the managed set so no two projects are due in the
   same idle cycle. Each entry gets a unique `time` within a documented window
   (away from the 06:05 standup slot), and its `lastTriggeredAt` seed offsets its
   `intervalDays` cycle by a project-index-derived amount. The scheme is
   deterministic for a given managed-root list and clock (injectable `--now`
   for tests), documented, and covered by tests asserting no duplicate `time`
   values and evenly spread day offsets.
4. Each scheduled run writes
   `<project-root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md` and
   `test_churn_data.json`; a re-run on the same date deterministically
   overwrites those two files and creates no duplicate files or directories.
5. Failures are surfaced: an inaccessible, non-git, or analyser-error root
   produces a non-zero exit code and a per-root error line on stderr (plus a
   run summary), and is never reported as a silent success.
6. The interval is configurable per entry in `scheduled-prompts.json` and via a
   provisioning `--interval-days` flag; the default (**7 days, weekly**) is
   documented in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` with its rationale.
7. Automated tests cover: entry provisioning (insert, preserve other entries,
   idempotent re-run, create-if-absent including an absent file, malformed or
   invalid config), staggering (unique `time`, spread day offsets, no
   re-stagger on re-run), managed-root iteration (existing, absent and non-git
   roots), date-partitioned output and idempotent overwrite, and non-zero
   failure propagation.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md`, `README.md`, and
   `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` (default interval, staggering and
   rationale).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Decisions (producer, 2026-11-01)

- **Q1 — fan-out shape: Option A.** One `/skill:test-churn` entry in each
  managed project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, with start times varied
  per project to prevent CPU blocking.
- **Q2 — managed-root source: Option A.** A checked-in managed-root list in
  SorraAgents. Tableau-Card-Engine must be given a schedule file
  (create-if-absent). The stale `open_source_llm` root is removed by a separate
  work item, **SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ**.
- **Q3 — default interval: Option A (7 days, weekly)**, with the day and time
  varied per project.

## Constraints

- `.worklog/` is ignored via `.worklog/*` in SorraAgents (the
  `scheduled-prompts.json` file is tracked despite that); the file lives
  per-project. The worktree-isolation rule forbids editing sibling projects'
  files from the SorraAgents worktree, so cross-project provisioning must be a
  tracked helper executed at dispatch time (or an explicit operator step), not
  a set of sibling-file edits in the implementation commit.
- The herdr downtime worker reads the file per root, dispatches one due entry
  per idle slot in config order, and only during a local-LLM idle window. The
  schedule is best-effort, not a hard cron. No changes to the external
  `worklog`/herdr package are in scope.
- The dispatcher has a host-CPU gate; several `test-churn` runs starting
  together would each scan long git histories and could block dispatch.
  Staggering (AC3) is required, not optional.
- The `time` window should avoid the existing `/skill:standup` slot (06:05) and
  stay inside a documented off-peak window.
- Dispatcher-managed roots currently recorded in
  `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` are: AI_Hell,
  ContextHub, SorraAgents, Tableau-Card-Engine, open_source_llm (stale — no
  longer exists), tce-main-street, ToneForge, tce-the-rising,
  podcast-building-games. The checked-in managed-root list is authoritative for
  this item; stale-root cleanup is SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ.
- The scheduled-prompt config is fail-closed in the consumer: absent or
  malformed config yields no dispatch and invalid entries are skipped.
  Provisioning must preserve unknown/invalid entries rather than rewrite the
  file.
- The analyser is read-only against each analysed repository but runs `git`
  per root, which can be slow on long histories; a run must bound itself
  (`--since` / `--max-commits`) or accept the cost.
- Tests must be run through the test skill (`/skill:test`); direct `pytest` or
  `node --test` invocations are prohibited.

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/` exists with `SKILL.md`,
  `scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` and `tests/`. The analyser already supports
  `--project-root`, `--output-dir`, `--report-name`, `--json-name`, `--since`,
  `--max-commits`, `--branch`, `--format`, `--stdout`, `--quiet`, and returns 1
  on `GitError`.
- SorraAgents `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` currently has `/skill:refactor`
  (3 days) and `/skill:standup` (1 day, 06:05).
- Scheduled-prompt ownership: schema and dispatch semantics live in the
  external `worklog` package (`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`;
  documented in its `CONFIG.md` § Scheduled-prompts config). `wl init`
  provisions a base file create-if-absent.
- Tableau-Card-Engine has a `.worklog/` directory but **no**
  `scheduled-prompts.json`.
- The stale `open_source_llm` root exists only as a cursor entry in
  `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`; its directory is gone.
- No scheduling, fan-out, or managed-root config exists for `test-churn`, and
  no documentation mentions periodic test-churn runs.
- `reports/` already exists at the SorraAgents repo root.

## Desired change

1. Add a tracked managed-root list (e.g. `skill/test-churn/managed-roots.json`)
   seeded from the dispatcher roots, excluding the stale `open_source_llm`.
2. Add
   `skill/test-churn/scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py`, which for each
   configured root inserts
   `{ "id": "/skill:test-churn", "prompt": "/skill:test-churn",
   "intervalDays": 7 }` create-if-absent into its
   `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, preserving all existing entries and
   `lastTriggeredAt`. It assigns a unique `time` per project (documented
   off-peak window, e.g. 02:00 + 40-minute steps) and a staggered
   `lastTriggeredAt` seed derived from the project index and the interval, so
   projects fall due on different days and times. It supports `--root`
   (repeatable), `--interval-days`, `--dry-run` and `--now` (tests).
3. Add `/skill:test-churn` to SorraAgents' `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`
   with the same staggering rules.
4. Add a thin wrapper (or documented invocation) so a scheduled run writes
   `<root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md` and
   `test_churn_data.json`, overwriting the same date idempotently and exiting
   non-zero on failure.
5. Tests and docs per the acceptance criteria.
6. Reference **SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ** for removing the stale `open_source_llm`
   cursor entry (out of scope here).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — add a "Scheduled runs" section (enable/disable,
  interval, staggering, output path, failure behaviour).
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/run_scheduled.py` — NEW wrapper: resolve the root,
  write the dated output directory, propagate the analyser exit code.
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py` — NEW idempotent
  provisioning with deterministic staggering.
- `skill/test-churn/managed-roots.json` — NEW authoritative managed-root list.
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_scheduled_runs.py` — NEW tests for provisioning,
  staggering, root iteration, dated output/idempotency and failure propagation.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — add the SorraAgents entry.
- `README.md` — mention/link the scheduled-run setup.
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — default interval, staggering
  scheme and rationale.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: CPU blocking.** Simultaneous whole-history scans across roots could
  trip the dispatcher's host-CPU gate. *Mitigation:* mandatory deterministic
  staggering of day and time per project (AC3), plus optional
  `--max-commits`/`--since` bounds.
- **Risk: worktree isolation.** Committing sibling projects' `.worklog` files
  from the SorraAgents worktree is forbidden. *Mitigation:* ship a tracked
  helper; do not edit sibling worklogs in the implementation commit.
- **Risk: silent staleness.** A project with no report looks healthy.
  *Mitigation:* per-root failure summary, non-zero exit, and the date in the
  output path.
- **Risk: schedule is best-effort.** It depends on an idle window, so reports
  may be late. *Mitigation:* document as best-effort; the interval gate
  prevents over-firing.
- **Risk: staggering drift.** A new project appended to the list could shift
  every entry's assigned slot. *Mitigation:* never re-stagger an existing entry;
  assign new roots the next free slot deterministically.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Integrating test-churn into `/skill:refactor` is a
  separate item (SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC). *Mitigation:* keep this item to
  registration, provisioning and scheduled execution only.
- **Assumption:** the managed-root list is the authoritative "all projects" set
  for this item; the live dispatcher root set may differ until the stale root
  is cleaned up.

## Related work

### Prerequisites / precedent

- **SA-0MV28WNFY009DF6Y** (completed epic) — migrated test-churn into
  SorraAgents and made reporting reproducible. The stated dependency is met.
- **SA-0MV28WS5G004YNNS** (completed) — created the reproducible test-churn
  reporting skill and its entry point.
- **SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW** (completed) — fixed status detection and the
  rewrite-ratio denominator.
- **SA-0MV28WXPA003EHJC** (completed) — added the tests-added/deleted growth
  metric that the scheduled report carries.
- **SA-0MV28WROY007NAB4** (completed) — ported the analysis tooling and data.

### Discovered / out of scope

- **SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ** (open, discovered-from this item) — remove the stale
  `open_source_llm` root from the herdr downtime round-robin cursor.
- **SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC** (open) — integrate test-churn into the refactor
  skill and its report. Separate scope; this item only schedules the skill.
- **SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO** (open) — complete the test-value refactor (prune
  tests that do not earn their runtime). Consumes the same growth metrics.
- **SA-0MTYIMWQP0020ZUC** (completed) — test execution policy; scheduled runs
  and tests must respect it.

### Automated related-work report

The `find-related` sweep added: SA-0MTWO7HFW001N9QJ (standup report title),
SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG (rebuild step in implement SKILL), SA-0MUMHH4BB000WEM9
(refactor report title). These are weak/report-formatting matches, not
duplicates. No completed item satisfies this item's acceptance criteria, so no
duplicate close was performed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

### Q1 — Fan-out shape

**Question:** Should the schedule use (A) one `/skill:test-churn` entry in each
managed project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, or (B) a single SorraAgents
entry whose prompt runs a fan-out command across all managed roots?

**Recommended:** A — per-project entries match the existing `/skill:refactor`
and `/skill:standup` pattern, spread analysis load across each root's idle
window, and avoid one very long-running pane.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-01):** **A** — per-project entries, and be sure to
vary the start time per project to prevent CPU blocking. Source: interactive
reply. Recorded as AC3 (staggering) and the CPU-blocking risk.

### Q2 — Managed-root source

**Question:** Which set of projects counts as "all projects": (A) a new checked-in
managed-root list in SorraAgents, (B) the dispatcher's live
`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`, or (C) auto-discover every
git repository under `~/projects` that has a `.worklog/`?

**Recommended:** A — a checked-in list is deterministic, reviewable and testable;
the live round-robin file is runtime state that includes a stale/missing root
and can change without review.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-01):** **A** — checked-in managed-root list; give
Tableau-Card-Engine a schedule file, and create a work item to remove the stale
item (`open_source_llm`). Source: interactive reply. Tableau-Card-Engine
create-if-absent is AC2; the stale-root removal is
**SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ**.

### Q3 — Default interval

**Question:** What default `intervalDays` should the entry ship with: (A) 7
(weekly), (B) 30 (monthly), or (C) 1 (daily)?

**Recommended:** A (weekly) — the report trends test growth per calendar quarter,
so weekly captures a regression promptly without consuming an idle slot every
day; it is overridable per entry and via `--interval-days`.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-01):** **A (7 days, weekly)**, with the day and time
varied per project. Source: interactive reply. Recorded in AC3/AC6 and the
default-interval documentation requirement (AC8).

### Duplicate check

Duplicate-work detection was performed (`wl search test-churn`,
`wl search "scheduled prompts"`, `wl search "test churn"`). No completed item
satisfies this item's acceptance criteria; the closest overlapping item,
SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC, integrates test-churn into the refactor report and is
explicitly out of scope here.

# Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically (shared /tmp report path / concurrent agents)

## Problem statement

The ship skill's post-release branch cleanup (`runPostReleaseCleanup` in
`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) fails non-deterministically in a
multi-agent (herdr) environment because it reads and writes a **fixed shared
temp path** (`${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json`): when two release/cleanup
processes run concurrently, one clobbers the other's report, so the run logs
"Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.", then silently
reports "Found 0 merged local branch(es)" and "Pruned 0 local branch(es)" as
if the repository were clean, and the follow-on remote prune also fails.
Observed during the AI_Hell v0.1.10 dev→main release; the same scripts succeed
when re-run standalone.

## Users

- **Agents (Map / herdr):** run automated releases and must not be misled by a
  false "clean" cleanup results.
- **Operators:** trust that post-release cleanup either happened or produced an
  actionable, non-silent warning.
- **Other projects consuming the shared ship/cleanup skills** (AI_Hell, etc.):
  any project can hit the race when releases coincide.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a **unique temp path per run** (e.g. derived from
   `mkdtempSync`) for the summarize report; a unit test with two
   concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py` run or report read no longer silently
   reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct,
   actionable warning naming the deterministic remediation (unique temp path).
3. The cleanup stays **non-blocking**: a cleanup failure never changes the
   release exit code (existing AC3 preserved).
4. A transient failure (summarize run / report read / remote prune) is
   **retried once** before the actionable warning is emitted.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **SorraAgents** repo (ship/cleanup skills are symlinked
  from `~/.pi/agent/skills` into `SorraAgents/skill/`); AI_Hell does not vendor
  these files.
- Cleanup scripts' standalone behaviour (`summarize_branches.py`,
  `prune_local_branches.py`, `delete_remote_branches.py`) must not change.
- Non-blocking guarantee must be preserved (existing AC3 of
  SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG).
- Tests run under `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json` to
`summarize_branches.py --report` (~L1110) and reads it back (~L1135). On read
failure it sets `reportData = { branches: [] }` and logs only the generic
"skipping local cleanup" warning, then proceeds to report "Found 0 merged local
branch(es)". The branches-to-delete file already uses `mkdtempSync`
(`cleanup-branches-*`), so only the report path is shared.

## Desired change

- Derive a unique report path per run (mkdtemp-based) used for both the
  `--report` argument and the read-back, so concurrent runs cannot clobber.
- Distinguish a real "no merged branches" result from a failed enumerate/read:
  log an actionable warning (unique-path remediation) instead of the misleading
  "0 merged branches".
- Add a single retry with small backoff for the transient step(s) before
  emitting the warning, preserving non-blocking behaviour.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` with the concurrency-clobber
  test and report-failure-warning test.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `runPostReleaseCleanup` (report path
  L1110/L1135, retry logic, warning text)
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` — new AC1 concurrency fake test,
  AC2 warning test, AC4 retry test

## Risks & assumptions

- **Retry must not mask real errors** — the single retry is for transient
  failures only; the actionable warning must still be emitted on the second
  failure (assumption: failures are quiet enough to retry once without
  doubling wall-clock time; mitigation: small backoff).
- **Scope creep** — deeper cleanup-skill refactoring, branch-deletion policy
  changes, or fixing `delete_remote_branches.py`/`summarize_branches.py`
  behaviour are out of scope; if such work is discovered, record it as new
  linked work items (not here).
- **Test isolation** — the concurrency test must not touch the real
  `/tmp/cleanup-summary.json` or run real git commands; fakes only
  (assumption: existing `setupRunReleaseFixture` harness is reused/adapted).
- **Cross-repo tracking** — item originated in the AI_Hell worklog
  (AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU, moved here per producer decision Q1c); AI_Hell leaves
  no orphan reference after deletion.
- **Non-blocking guarantee** — AC3 must survive the retry addition; the retry
  must also be non-blocking.

## Related work

- SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG — Automate post-release cleanup (introduced this code).
- AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ — Discord notification fails (precedent: ship-skill bug
  tracked in AH worklog, fixed in SorraAgents).

# Audit runner: Phase 2 deep-analysis timeout diagnostic hardcodes CALL_PI_TIMEOUT

`discovered-from:LP-0MV81ZIL8008RS9J` — found while auditing that item.

## Problem statement

The audit runner's Phase 2 deep-analysis failure path reports a **hardcoded
timeout** regardless of the actual abort cause, making infra stalls
indistinguishable from budget exhaustion and undermining operator diagnostics.

In `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, the Phase 2 timeout branch always
raises:

```python
RuntimeError(f"Phase 2 deep analysis timed out after {CALL_PI_TIMEOUT}s")  # line ~7669
```

`CALL_PI_TIMEOUT` is the constant `1800` (line 547). This fires even when an
explicit `--timeout` (e.g. `2700`) or `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT` (e.g. `1500`)
override is in effect, because the message never consults the resolved
effective timeout (`_resolve_call_timeout`, line ~4118) or the stall detector's
resolved value (`_resolve_stall_timeout`, line ~2703).

## Observed impact (LP-0MV81ZIL8008RS9J)

Three consecutive audit runs (~60 min wall-clock each) stalled identically at
"Phase 2 deep analysis" while the shared local LLM proxy was saturated (0/3
slots free; 57k–73k-token generations in flight). In each run:

- The per-call Pi invocation did stream *something* (Phase 1 parent screens and
  verdict re-asks completed and parsed fine), but the long tool-enabled deep
  call produced no output within the stall window.
- The persisted report and the `--json` `script_failure.reason` both claimed
  "Phase 2 deep analysis timed out after 1800s" — even on the run launched with
  `--timeout 2700` + `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT=1500`.
- Because the diagnostic cannot distinguish (a) staleness/no-output vs
  (b) effective-budget exhaustion, the operator cannot tell whether to raise
  the budget, raise the stall window, or wait for proxy capacity. The audit
  had to fail closed with a fallback notice (`Ready to close: No`, non-authoritative).

## Root cause

`_run_phase2_deep_analysis` does thread the resolved timeout through to the Pi
call correctly (`_call_pi_and_maybe_log(..., timeout=timeout, ...)` →
`_resolve_call_timeout`), so overrides DO extend the call. It is only the
**failure diagnostic** that hardcodes the constant, hiding the effective values
from the operator and from the persisted report.

## Desired change

Make the Phase 2 timeout abort report the **actual** values that fired:

1. The resolved effective per-call timeout used for the deep call
   (`--timeout` / `AUDIT_PI_TIMEOUT` override, else `CALL_PI_TIMEOUT`).
2. The resolved stall detector timeout (`AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT`, else 600).
3. Which mechanism aborted the call: stall (no output for Ns) vs effective
   budget (N s) — surfaced in stderr, the persisted audit report, and the
   `--json` `script_failure` payload.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** `--timeout N` / `AUDIT_PI_TIMEOUT=N` is reflected verbatim in the
   Phase 2 timeout diagnostic (`script_failure.reason`, stderr, persisted
   report) — never the hardcoded 1800s when an override is in effect.
2. **AC2:** `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT=S` is reflected in the diagnostic when the
   stall detector aborts the deep call, and the stall abort is labelled
   distinctly from an effective-budget abort (e.g. "stalled: no output for Ss"
   vs "timed out after Ns").
3. **AC3:** With no overrides, behaviour is unchanged: deep calls still abort
   at the 1800s budget / 600s stall defaults, and the diagnostic still reports
   those defaults (no regression of LP-0MSQ32S2M001EA74).
4. **AC4:** Unit tests cover the diagnostic text for: stall abort with
   `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT` override, budget abort with `--timeout` override, and
   the default (no override) path — asserting the exact strings an operator
   would see in `script_failure.reason`.
5. **AC5:** Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 2 timeout branch (~line 7669),
  `_resolve_call_timeout` (~4118), `_resolve_stall_timeout` (~2703),
  `_call_pi` stall logic (~4130–4180), `CALL_PI_TIMEOUT` constant (~547).
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — report/`script_failure` persistence
  (verify the corrected diagnostic reaches the stored audit text).
- Audit skill tests covering Phase 2 timeout behaviour
  (e.g. `skill/audit/tests/` or `tests/unit/` for the runner).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: behaviour change in a safety-critical path** — the stall/budget abort
  itself is unchanged; only the diagnostic text changes. Mitigation: AC3/AC4
  pin the default behaviour and strings.
- **Assumption:** the underlying Phase 2 stall on a saturated proxy is expected
  behaviour (fail-closed, recoverable); this item only fixes observability so
  operators can reason about it. The `--timeout` plumbing itself is confirmed
  working — no changes needed there.

# Tracer bullet: hermetic-migration recipe + local `git()` wrappers

Parent: SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0

## Goal

Establish the canonical hermetic-git migration recipe end-to-end on the
smallest, lowest-risk helper group (the three local `git()` wrappers), so the
remaining clusters (F2-F5) apply a proven, documented pattern rather than
re-deriving it. This is the tracer bullet: it cuts through code, tests and
docs in one slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The local `git()` helpers in `tests/test_test_cache.py`,
  `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` and `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py`
  are replaced with `shared.git_sandbox` calls (`init_repo`, `commit_all`,
  `run_git`); no bare `subprocess.run(["git", …])` remains in these files.
- [ ] Each migrated repo builder (e.g. `git_repo`, `cache_repo`) has a
  behavioural regression test proving a leaked `GIT_DIR` cannot redirect it —
  the victim repository is unchanged and the fixture repository resolves under
  `tmp_path` — mirroring
  `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py::TestEnvironmentIsolation` and
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py::TestRepoHelpersAreHermetic`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any `docs/dev/` entries such as `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` gains a "Migration recipe" section
  documenting the before/after pattern (factory + injected identity +
  containment assertion) and the regression-test template, so later features
  have a single reference.
- [ ] All existing assertions in the three files pass unchanged (no asserted
  behaviour changes; only the git execution path).

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace the module-level `git()` wrapper in each file with `gs.run_git`, and
  build each throwaway repo with `gs.init_repo(..., default_branch=…)` +
  `gs.commit_all(...)`.
- Add one hermetic regression test per migrated builder, using a victim repo
  and `monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_DIR", …)`, asserting the victim HEAD is
  unchanged and the fixture toplevel is under `tmp_path`.
- Append the migration recipe section to `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_test_cache.py`
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`
- `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py`
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`

## Dependencies

None (tracer bullet — must land first).

discovered-from:RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK

## Problem

The implement skill's Step 9 'belt-and-suspenders' post-push verification (/skill:test against the dev checkout) can resolve to a **cache hit and execute zero fresh tests**, while still looking like a green verification.

Observed end-to-end on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK:
1. implement.py finish runs the full suite (changed-scope, then --scope full) **inside the worktree**, stores green entries keyed by git state + scope in the per-repo test cache (2h TTL).
2. implement.py pushes from the worktree. In this repo the pre-push hook is a worklog-sync hook that exits 0 for worktrees (line ~80) — no test execution happens at push time.
3. The skill then says run /skill:test post-push. Because the cache key is git state + scope only, the main checkout's lookup at the same commit hits the entry stored by the finish gate. Both suite commands returned CACHED exit=0 — the final verification ran nothing.
4. Worse: the worktree environment can differ from the main checkout in ways the cache cannot see — on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK the core submodule failed to clone in the worktree ('transport file not allowed') and was populated manually; node_modules is symlinked. A green run recorded in the worktree is not proof the canonical checkout passes.

## Desired behaviour

- The post-push verification step must either (a) execute a genuinely fresh run against the canonical checkout when the push originated in a worktree (or when env differs), or (b) be made explicitly targeted for narrow changes (--scope changed --force) instead of a bare /skill:test that is cache-servable.
- The cache key should include enough environment/worktree identity that a worktree-recorded run cannot satisfy a main-checkout verification, OR implement.py finish should record whether the push came from a worktree so the post-push step knows to force a refresh.
- Keep fast iteration cheap: for narrow, well-covered changes, a forced changed-scope run is acceptable post-push evidence; reserve forced full runs for broad/refactor changes or environment drift (submodules, node_modules).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — After implement.py finish pushes from a worktree, a post-push verification on the main checkout executes a fresh run (it cannot be served from the cache entry recorded inside the worktree) for the affected scope.
- AC2 — A bare /skill:test post-push no longer silently returns 'green' from a cache populated by an in-worktree finish gate without executing: either the step force-refreshes, or the implement skill's Step 9 is updated to specify an explicit scope/force invocation (and documents when a forced full run is required vs a targeted one).
- AC3 — The per-repo test cache key (or its consumer logic in run_tests.py / implement.py) captures worktree-vs-main-checkout identity (e.g. git common dir, worktree path, or submodule status) so an in-worktree run and a main-checkout run for the same commit produce distinct entries.
- AC4 — Fast iteration is preserved: targeted post-push runs (--scope changed --force) remain the default for narrow changes; the full forced suite runs only when the change is broad, a refactor, or environment drift (submodule/node_modules) is detected.
- AC5 — Documented in implement SKILL.md Step 9 (and audit skill F3/F4 notes where relevant) with the exact commands; regression test in tests/ where the cache layer is tested.

## Constraints

- Do not break existing 2h-TTL caching for the audit skill's read-only full-suite verification — it still needs to query cached full runs at the same commit.
- Pre-existing framework items may partially intersect: SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (document pre-push bypass + verification recipe), SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (live-repo guard + push timeout). Reconcile rather than duplicate.
- Target files (from the live symlink tree /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills -> /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill): skill/test_cache.py (cache key), skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py (scope/force), skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (push origin record / verification step), skill/implement/SKILL.md (Step 9 wording), skill/audit/SKILL.md (F3/F4 notes if needed).

## Evidence

- Final /skill:test on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK: both suites reported CACHED exit=0 scope=full, i.e. no fresh execution.
- Worktree push: pre-push hook exits 0 for worktrees (saw line ~80 'exit 0' in .git/hooks/pre-push); submodule 'core' failed to clone in the worktree and was populated manually.

## Acceptance criteria

3. **AC3 - Drift impossible**: the documented 'host timeout matches queue timeout / stays inside parent bash-tool timeout' invariant is enforced by the shared definition, not by a comment.
4. **AC4 - Docs**: audit-skill reference and test-skill reference point at the shared module for wait-budget tuning.

## Goal

The test skill's paced_runner() already accepts an on_wait callback (queued_at, wait_seconds) and implement.py logs a pacing line, but there is no structured, queryable record of how often suite runs wait on the test/audit semaphores, how long they wait, and how often the bounded wait expires (TestConcurrencyTimeout / audit timeout). Tuning TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY, TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT, AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT and AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT is therefore guesswork. Without telemetry the deadlock class tracked by SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF / SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 can regress invisibly.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - Structured wait metrics**: every semaphore acquire wait on the 'test' and 'audit' namespaces (Semaphore.acquire in skill/shared/process_semaphore.py) records a structured event (name, max_workers, queued_at, acquired_at, wait_seconds, deadline_expired flag) to a stable JSON-lines location, e.g. a per-run or per-host file under a configurable directory.
2. **AC2 - Timeout events captured**: TestConcurrencyTimeout (run_tests.py) and audit timeout verdicts are recorded with the same schema (no new exceptions, no behaviour change).
3. **AC3 - Read-only aggregation**: a helper (e.g. skill/shared/contention_summary.py) aggregates the recorded events into a human/JSON summary (percentiles of wait, timeout counts, slot-saturation histogram) without acquiring any semaphore.
4. **AC4 - Documented tuning feedback**: docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md describe how to use the telemetry to tune the ceiling/timeout env vars; the full project test suite passes with the change.
5. **AC5 - Opt-out and boundedness**: telemetry is cheap (append-only, per-event timestamp), never blocks the acquire path, and can be disabled with an env var; tests run in temp dirs (PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR isolation preserved).

## Constraints

- Recording must not add latency to the acquire path (no blocking I/O in the wait loop; write asynchronously or after the wait resolves).
- No behavioural change to concurrency semantics: ceiling, timeout, nested-run isolation and cache-hit bypass all unchanged.
- Respect PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR isolation in tests so telemetry files never collide with the host-wide pool.

## Related work

- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG - test skill shared concurrency primitive (defines ceiling/timeout)
- SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF - multi-agent audit/test coordination (the deadlock class this telemetry makes observable)
- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 - nested-run semaphore isolation (PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR contract to honour in telemetry paths)
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 - pacing telemetry (on_wait callback; existing partial hook)

## Goal

Nested-run isolation (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) works only when a test fixture explicitly sets PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR to an isolated directory via nested_semaphore_dir(). Any NEW test that spawns a subprocess running run_tests.py (or invokes the runner in-process) silently re-enters the host-wide 'test' pool and can deadlock exactly as before: the outer run holds a slot the nested run waits behind until TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT. The LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE recursion marker already solves the analogous problem for the live-repo guard (subprocesses inherit it; nested guards stand down). The test semaphore has no equivalent, so the fix depends on every future test author remembering an opt-in convention.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - Automatic isolation marker**: a run that holds a host-wide 'test' slot exports an inherited marker (e.g. TEST_SEMAPHORE_SLOT_HELD=1) to its subprocess environment; the marker is set/cleared by the same code that acquires/releases the slot (run_tests.py's _test_concurrency_slot), so it cannot drift from the real acquisition.
2. **AC2 - Nested runs auto-isolate**: when run_tests.py detects the marker already set (i.e. it is a nested invocation), it derives an isolated namespace automatically (e.g. a per-invocation directory under the marker's parent, or nested_semaphore_dir of a run-scoped root) instead of contending for the host-wide pool — no fixture opt-in required.
3. **AC3 - Explicit override still wins**: an explicitly-set PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR always takes precedence over the automatic derivation, so existing fixtures and operators keep full control.
4. **AC4 - Host-wide ceiling preserved**: top-level runs (marker absent) still bound themselves via TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY; only nested invocations isolate.
5. **AC5 - Regression test**: a test spawns a nested run_tests.py WITHOUT setting PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR while an outer slot is held, and asserts it completes without waiting on the host-wide pool (and that an explicit PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR still wins).
6. **AC6 - Docs**: docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/test-isolation.md document the automatic marker as the default contract (the fixture helper remains available); full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- The marker must be inherited by subprocesses only through the normal env chain — no global mutation of the parent's own environment (mirror the LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE pattern).
- Nested isolation must not weaken host-wide bounding for genuine parallel suites.
- Do not break existing fixtures that already set PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR explicitly (explicit wins).
- Full project test suite must pass.

## Related work

- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 - introduced nested_semaphore_dir() + opt-in PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR isolation (this item makes it the default)
- SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H / SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q - LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE recursion marker (the pattern to mirror)
- SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO - contention telemetry (complementary observability)

## Goal (discovered during SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD)

The per-repo test cache (skill/test_cache.py) dedupes *completed* runs at the same git state (2h TTL), but two agents that both miss the cache at the identical command + git state execute the full suite **concurrently** (both acquire a slot when TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY >= 2; the second duplicates work the first is already doing). With nested-run isolation (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) now making the host-wide 'test' pool the only contention point, the next structural reduction is single-flight: the second caller should wait on the first in-flight run's result instead of acquiring its own slot and re-running.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - In-flight markers**: a run that misses the cache publishes an in-flight marker keyed by (normalized command, git state, scope, test_type) before executing and clears it on completion (including crash/timeout paths).
2. **AC2 - Coalescing**: a second caller that finds a fresh in-flight marker for the identical key waits for that run's stored result (bounded by TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT) instead of executing a duplicate; if the marker goes stale (holder died) the caller proceeds normally.
3. **AC3 - No correctness change**: cache hits/stores/TTL/scope/test_type semantics are unchanged; a coalesced caller receives the identical result dict shape as a cache miss+run (with a marker such as coalesced: true) so downstream consumers are unaffected.
4. **AC4 - Bounded, no new deadlock**: coalescing never blocks past TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT and cannot deadlock (stale markers expire; a crashed holder is detectable by marker age/pid).
5. **AC5 - Tests**: deterministic tests cover (a) two callers with the same key execute once, (b) different keys still execute independently, (c) a stale marker does not block, (d) cache hits bypass coalescing.
6. **AC6 - Docs + full suite**: test-skill reference documents the coalescing contract; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Must not weaken the two-slot host-wide ceiling (this reduces duplicate work, not the ceiling).
- Single-flight must be per-repo (and worktree-aware), honouring the existing git-state fingerprint.
- Full project test suite must pass (build -> test -> commit order).

## Related work

- SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD - staggered back-off (this item's parent discovery; complementary — stave off the herd, then coalesce its redundant members)
- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 - nested-run isolation (makes the top-level pool pure)
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 - pacing telemetry (on_wait) - the coalesced wait should reuse it
- SA-0MVEDMM3N004Y6MO - contention telemetry (observability for coalescing effectiveness)

## Goal

Refine the audit stage's acceptance of full-suite evidence: matching-git-state GREEN cached entries are accepted **without a practical time bound** (code identity is already guaranteed by the git-state key), so audit re-runs never occur purely because evidence is old. Red entries keep the existing 5-minute failed-run expiry.

## Problem (discovered-from:SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81)

SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 shipped `AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 24h` as the audit's acceptance window. The operator's challenge is valid: the full suite was proven green by the dev-push gate at the pushed commit; the cache key is the byte-identical git state, so the wall clock adds nothing about the CODE. Environment drift (deps/infra/host state) is the only thing a time bound hedges, and it is already caught fresh at the next dev-push and by the enforced ship release gate (AC4) before anything ships. A 24h expiry therefore causes needless F3 full-suite re-runs (slot contention) for re-audits, backlogs and HEAD-drifted audits with no safety gain.

## Requirements

1. Replace the 24h audit acceptance with a no-practical-bound semantics for GREEN entries (e.g. an explicitly documented large `AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, or an explicit green-never-expires mode in the audit's lookup); non-zero-exit entries remain capped at the 5-minute failed-run TTL (`lookup()` already applies `min(ttl, FAILED_RUN_TTL_SECONDS)`).
2. Pin the semantics with tests: a green entry backdated well beyond 24h (e.g. 120 days) still classifies GREEN; a green entry beyond the generic 2h TTL is NOT a miss; a failed entry still expires at 5 minutes.
3. Update skill/audit/SKILL.md and docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md (remove the "24h acceptance window" language).
4. F3 (auto-execute on genuine miss) and F4 (never-block) behaviour unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A green full-suite entry backdated 120 days at a matching git state classifies as AUTO-VERIFIED GREEN (no F3 execution).
- AC2: A failed (non-zero) entry still expires after the 5-minute TTL and is never accepted as evidence.
- AC3: Audit docs no longer describe a time-based acceptance window for green entries; they state green evidence at a matching git state is accepted without a practical time bound (grep-verifiable).
- AC4: All tests pass via the test skill (changed-scope and the audit test group); changes committed and pushed to dev.
data.title: Audit: accept matching-state green full-suite evidence without a practical time bound

## Goal

Make the changed-scope test gate run the **union of all matching skill groups**, not a single arbitrary pick, and align the two selectors (implement.py `run_tests` and `run_tests.py --scope changed`) on the same semantics.

## Problem (discovered-from:SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81)

`select_group_from_changed_files` returns the single group with the fewest commands; when multiple groups match with equal command counts, `min(matching, key=matching.get)` returns an arbitrary one (insertion order). A cross-skill change — e.g. touching `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**` and `skill/audit/**` simultaneously, exactly like SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 — therefore gate-tests only ONE of the affected skill suites pre-commit, deferring the rest to the push-time full gate (and the import-graph selector cannot cover them: `map_changed_to_tests` only scans root `tests/`/`test/` dirs, not skill-group test dirs). The run_tests.py CLI's `--scope changed` uses a different (file-level) selector than implement.py's group-first selector, so the two agree only by accident.

## Requirements

1. A changed set matching N groups (e.g. implement + test + audit) runs the commands of ALL N groups exactly once (deduplicated), with each suite's cache key/type metadata preserved (`group:<name>`).
2. Matching-group selection becomes deterministic and documented (union by paths; no arbitrary single pick). When no group matches, behaviour falls back to the existing file-level selector / full suite unchanged.
3. implement.py `run_tests(scope="changed")` and `run_tests.py --scope changed` converge on the same group-union semantics (single source of truth for group selection).
4. Per-command timeouts account for N groups (a multi-group run must not blow the 600s default); cache entries remain distinct per group.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A change touching `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**` and `skill/audit/**` invokes all three groups' suite commands in a `--scope changed` run.
- AC2: A group matching multiple changed files runs once (no duplicate commands).
- AC3: The CLI (`run_tests.py --scope changed`) and `implement.py` finish select the same command set for the same changed set (convergence test).
- AC4: No group match → existing fallback behaviour unchanged (file-level selection, then full).
- AC5: All tests pass via the test skill; changes committed and pushed to dev.
data.title: Changed-scope gate: run the union of all matching test groups (fix single-group pick) and align selectors

## Goal

Unify the per-repo test-cache namespace across git worktrees and the main checkout so evidence produced in either checkout is reusable from the other (no duplicate full-suite runs at the same git state caused purely by the namespace split).

## Problem (discovered-from:SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81)

`test_cache.cache_dir()` resolves per checkout: a worktree looks for a worktree-local `.worklog` (created by `implement.py start`) → `<worktree>/.worklog/cache`, else `git rev-parse --git-dir`/`test-cache` — which for linked worktrees is `<main>/.git/worktrees/<name>/test-cache`, a DIFFERENT namespace from the main checkout's `<main>/.worklog/cache`. Consequence: a changed-scope run cached inside a worktree is invisible to the pre-push hook / audit / belt-and-suspenders running from the main checkout and vice versa. Under the new regime (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81: full suite first runs at the dev-push gate in the main checkout), aligning the namespaces lets worktree gate evidence and main-checkout gate evidence share one store — eliminating a class of duplicate full runs and stale-miss F3/F5 auto-executions.

## Requirements

1. `cache_dir()` resolves a SINGLE namespace for a worktree and its main checkout — e.g. prefer the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` (resolve via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), or a shared `<git-common-dir>/test-cache`, falling back to the current rules for non-git/non-linked layouts.
2. Writes stay atomic (they already are: temp file + `os.replace`); concurrent writers from two checkouts must not corrupt entries.
3. Repos without worktrees keep the current behaviour byte-for-byte; the audit's read-only `query_cached()` and other consumers are unaffected API-wise.
4. Tests cover: a run cached in a worktree is a hit from the main checkout at the same git state (and vice versa); worktree-local `.worklog` presence no longer forks the namespace.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A suite cached from inside a linked worktree is served from the main checkout's `run_tests.py --summary` at the same git state, and the reverse direction also hits.
- AC2: A non-worktree repo (plain clone) resolves the cache exactly as today (byte-identical path resolution).
- AC3: 2 concurrent writers (worktree + main) at the same key leave a valid entry (no torn write).
- AC4: All tests pass via the test skill (test_cache suite + affected consumers); changes committed and pushed to dev.
data.title: Unify test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout

# Refactor skill: detect files > 1000 lines and file refactor work items

## Problem statement

The refactor skill detects `god_class` and `long_method` via LLM judgement, but
has **no deterministic file-size signal**. Files therefore grow far past a
readable size unnoticed: the ContextHub repo sweep that produced
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts, 8,205 lines) found **15 production
files over 1,000 lines** — `worklist.ts` 7,792, `database.ts` 3,684,
`index.ts` 2,784 and eleven more — none of which the skill had ever flagged.

File length is a cheap, objective, language-independent maintainability proxy
and belongs in the skill's default rule set, not in ad-hoc producer sweeps.

## Users

- **Producers/agents running `/skill:refactor`** want oversized files surfaced
  automatically instead of discovered by manual `wc -l` sweeps.
- **Maintainers** want a consistent 1,000-line ceiling applied across every
  project without re-deriving the rule each time.
- **Reviewers** want refactor work items to exist before a file becomes
  unmaintainable, with an explicit "is refactoring appropriate?" judgement
  recorded.

User stories:

- As a producer running a full-project refactor scan, I want every file over
  1,000 lines listed so that I can decide which to decompose.
- As an agent, I want a work item filed automatically when a large file
  genuinely warrants decomposition, so that the finding is not lost.

## Goal

Add a deterministic **file-length** smell to the refactor skill: any source file
over 1,000 lines is flagged, evaluated by the existing LLM smell-detection pass
for whether refactoring is appropriate, and — when appropriate — a Worklog work
item is created through the existing `workitem_creation` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A deterministic pre-LLM scan flags every tracked source file whose line
   count exceeds a configurable threshold (default 1,000), reporting
   path, line count and excess.
2. The threshold is configurable via `.refactor.json` (e.g.
   `"file_length": {"enabled": true, "threshold": 1000}`) and disabled when set
   to `0`/`false`; the default applies with no config present.
3. Over-threshold files are passed to the LLM evaluation step, which decides
   whether decomposition is appropriate and records a one-line rationale;
   files judged not to warrant decomposition are reported but create no work
   item.
4. For appropriate files, exactly one Worklog work item is created (tags
   `Refactor`), idempotently — re-running the scan does not create a duplicate
   (existing REFACTOR-comment and `wl list --tags Refactor` dedup guards apply).
5. Generated test files/vendored/generated paths are excluded from the
   threshold check, and the exclusion list is configurable.
6. Unit tests cover: over/under threshold, config override/disable, LLM
   "not appropriate" suppression, dedup on re-run, and exclusion patterns.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
   (`skill/refactor/SKILL.md` smell-type table and `.refactor.json` example).

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing rule/config plumbing (`smell_detection.DEFAULT_RULES`,
  `scripts/config.py`, `workitem_creation.create_smell_work_item`) rather than
  adding a parallel mechanism.
- Deterministic and offline: the line-count scan must work with the LLM
  disabled (report-only) and must not require a network call.
- No behavioural change to existing smell types or their severities.

## Desired change

- New `file_length` rule + deterministic detector feeding the existing smell
  pipeline; severity `medium` by default (high above ~2× threshold).
- LLM prompt extension: for `file_length` findings, answer "does this file have
  multiple separable concerns that warrant decomposition?" with a rationale.
- Work-item title format consistent with existing generated titles, e.g.
  `Refactor: decompose <path> god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines)`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/smell_detection.py` — add `file_length` to `DEFAULT_RULES`
  smell types and a deterministic line-count detector.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/config.py` — default config entry and threshold.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — wire the detector into the scan and
  pass findings to the LLM evaluation.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — ensure `file_length` titles/descriptions
  and dedup behave correctly.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document the new smell type, config key and
  exclusion defaults.
- `skill/refactor/tests/` — unit tests for AC1–AC6.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (ContextHub) — the downtime-worker.ts god-class item whose
  manual sweep exposed the gap: 15 production files over 1,000 lines, prompting
  the producer directive that every such file be evaluated and, if appropriate,
  given a refactor work item.
- ContextHub follow-up refactor items created from that sweep (worklist.ts,
  database.ts, persistent-store.ts ×2, index.ts, fetcher.ts,
  dispatcher-anchor.ts, downtime-log.ts, sync.ts, github.ts, github-sync.ts,
  interview.ts, doctor.ts, init.ts).

## Assumptions

- 1,000 lines is the default ceiling; projects may override it per repo.
- "Evaluated for refactoring and if appropriate a work item should be created"
  is implemented as an LLM judgement gate, not an unconditional filing, so the
  scan does not flood backlogs with items for unavoidably large generated or
  data-heavy modules.
- Test files are in scope for the check by default (large test suites also
  warrant decomposition); generated/vendored paths are excluded.
data.title: Refactor skill: detect files > 1000 lines, evaluate refactor need, and file work items
