# Port the post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite hooks to the repo-root v2 wrappers

**Headline:** The three committed Worklog hooks are `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1`
wrappers that `exec` an absolute per-machine path,
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. When that path is absent (any
machine where `scripts/install_pi.sh` has not run), every checkout, merge and
`git worktree add` fails with `exec: … not found` (exit 127) and the post-pull
`wl sync` never runs — which broke `wl sync` in this repository on 2026-10-30
until `scripts/install_pi.sh` was re-run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` closed the "nothing creates the central script" half of
the problem by installing it from `install_pi.sh`. The remaining half is the
hard-coded absolute path itself: the hooks only work on a machine where the
installer ran, and a relocation or a fresh host silently disables the Worklog
sync. `ContentCreator` already migrated its hooks to `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2`
wrappers that resolve the delegate from the repository root
(`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) and fail open; this repository still ships the
v1 form.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** — `implement.py start/finish` and `wl sync` abort
  with exit 127 whenever git creates a worktree or checks out a branch on a
  machine without the central hook.
- **Developers on a fresh clone or a renamed checkout** — merges error on a
  hook they did not write and cannot see.
- **Producers** — Worklog data silently stops syncing when the hook errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
      `.githooks/post-rewrite` carry the `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2` marker,
      resolve `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
      `cd` there, and `exec` it.
- [ ] All three wrappers are fail-open: no resolvable repository root, a missing
      delegate, or a missing `wl`/`worklog` exits 0 so a merge or checkout never
      fails because of the hook.
- [ ] `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` still short-circuits the sync (delegate
      behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Tests prove the hooks work with `$HOME` unset or pointing at a sandbox and
      without any `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, from the
      repository root and from a subdirectory, for all three wrappers.
- [ ] A test scans `.githooks/` and fails if any file regains a hard-coded
      absolute checkout path (the `ContentCreator` equivalent lives in
      `tests/test_worklog_hooks.py`).
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` no longer warns that the wrappers do not delegate
      to the central path, and either stops installing the central script or
      documents it as legacy.
- [ ] `docs/dev/` hook documentation describes the v2 wrappers and the fail-open
      contract.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `docs/dev/` hook pages.

## Constraints

- Keep `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as the single implementation of the
  post-pull sync; the wrappers stay thin.
- Do not change the pre-push hook or its gates.
- Removal of the central-script install from `install_pi.sh` is optional; if it
  stays, it must not be required for the hooks to work.

## Existing state

```
$ cat .githooks/post-checkout
#!/bin/sh
# worklog:post-pull-hook:v1
# Wrapper that delegates to central Worklog post-pull script (committed hooks).
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

Observed failure (2026-10-30, `wl sync` in this repository):

```
✗ Sync failed: Command failed with exit code 127: git worktree add --detach '…/.worklog/tmp-worktree-yZC0Kd/wt' 'refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data'
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD a07575c13)
/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
```

Running `scripts/install_pi.sh` created
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and the sync then succeeded — a
workaround, not a fix.

## Desired change

Replace the three v1 wrappers with the v2 wrapper (see
`ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge` for the canonical text), extend
`tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` (or a new hook test module) with the
`$HOME`-independent cases, and update `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the docs to
match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-merge` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-rewrite` — v2 wrapper
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — hook behaviour without the central
  script; hard-coded-path scan
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — stop requiring the central script; drop the
  delegation warning
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (or the equivalent hook page) — v2 wrapper
  contract

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` works when executed from the
  repository root; that is how `post-merge` already invokes it.
- **Risk (low):** a `post-checkout` run inside `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (the
  Worklog data branch) would sync from that temporary checkout. Mitigation: the
  delegate is already fail-open and warns on failure; verify it does not
  recurse when the temporary worktree has no `.worklog`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** consolidating the hooks with the ContentCreator copy
  into one shared installer is tempting. Record that separately; this item only
  ports the v2 wrapper shape.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — installs the central post-pull script (the other half
  of the same failure mode).
- `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` — fail-open portability warning added to
  `install_pi.sh`.
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` (ContentCreator) — the item whose `wl sync` surfaced
  this failure.
data.title: Port the post-checkout/post-merge/post-rewrite hooks to the repo-root v2 wrappers

# implement.py Key Files gate misses the bold-inside-heading form

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-31). That RISE item was filed during `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` and is deleted once this item exists (producer decision Q1 = re-file here).

**Headline:** The Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate in `implement.py` parses only
`## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)` and a bare `**Key Files:**` line, so a
work item whose section is written `## **Key Files:**` (bold marker nested in an
H2/H3) yields no key files, dirty-file relevance becomes unjudgeable, and
`implement.py start` aborts on a dirty checkout even when every dirty path is
unrelated. Make the heading matcher form-agnostic and lock it down with
regression tests.

## Problem statement

`_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` matches
`#{1,6}\s*Key Files.*` (heading) **or** `\*\*Key Files:?\*\*.*` (bold line) — but
not the combination `## **Key Files:**`, because after the `## ` prefix the next
token is `**`, not `Key Files`. `extract_key_files_from_description()` then
returns `[]`, `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` reports *"no Key Files section in
the work item description — cannot judge dirty-file relevance"*, and
`phase_start` takes the conservative abort-and-ask branch even though the
description does list key files and the dirty paths demonstrably do not overlap
them. The gate's conservative default is correct; it is being tripped by a
parser gap rather than by a real risk.

## Evidence

Reproduced in this session against the installed skill tree
(`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`):

| form | `extract_key_files_from_description` |
|---|---|
| `## Key Files` | `['a/b.ts', 'tests/c.test.ts']` |
| `## Key Files (predicted)` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `**Key Files:**` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `## **Key Files:**` | `[]` |
| `### **Key Files:**` | `[]` |

- **Corpus prevalence (consumer store):** 9 of 386 items in the
  `tce-the-rising` store use the bold-inside-heading form — the face-off tie
  epic parent RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight children
  (RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX, RISE-0MVRMI7GR006QH44, RISE-0MVRMI9F0007HXBW,
  RISE-0MVRMIB7Z008P1HB, RISE-0MVRMID1B0098HAY, RISE-0MVRMIF0T008A72W,
  RISE-0MVRMIGXS0073HDX, RISE-0MVRMIISC009TXYX). For comparison: 297 items use
  a plain heading, 52 a bare bold line, 28 none.
- **Observed stall:** `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` aborted on child
  RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX (Key Files: `tests/the-rising/risingMatchHarness.ts`,
  `tests/the-rising/TheRisingRules.test.ts`) although the only dirty paths were
  six untracked `standups/*.md` files — zero overlap, i.e. exactly the
  documented "proceed, leave the dirty files untouched" case. The operator
  worked around it by pre-creating the worktree and running `start` from inside
  it (where the main-checkout gate is skipped by design).
- **No direct test coverage** of `extract_key_files_from_description`,
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files` or `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` exists under
  `skill/implement/tests/`, so this class of gap is invisible to the suite.
- The framework does **not** emit the H2-wrapped form itself:
  `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` (`_parse_key_files_section`,
  `validate_key_files_format`) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` use a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line, so both families of form must keep working.

## Users

- **Implement-skill agent (primary)**: "When I start an item whose Key Files
  section is written `## **Key Files:**`, I want `start` to read those paths and
  let me proceed when the dirty files are unrelated, so I do not have to
  hand-work around a gate that already has the information it needs."
- **Producer / operator (secondary)**: "When a downtime run dispatches a child
  session, I want `start` to proceed or abort for a real reason, so unattended
  runs do not stall on a parsing bug."
- **Framework maintainer**: "I want every accepted Key Files heading form
  covered by a table-driven test, so a future edit to the extractor cannot
  silently drop a form."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `extract_key_files_from_description()` returns the listed paths for
  any `Key Files` heading regardless of emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or
  case: `## **Key Files:**`, `### **Key Files:**`, `## **Key Files (predicted):**`,
  `#### key files`, asserted by a table-driven unit test in
  `skill/implement/tests/`.
- **AC2** — Every currently supported form keeps working, asserted in the same
  table: `## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)`, `### Key Files`, and a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line; plus the tolerant bare-marker variants —
  `  **Key Files:**` (indented/whitespace) and `**Key Files**` (no colon).
- **AC3** — `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` proceeds (`can_proceed: true`)
  when the description uses `## **Key Files:**` and the dirty paths do not
  overlap those entries, and still aborts (`can_proceed: false`) when a dirty
  path does overlap, or when the description has no Key Files section at all.
- **AC4** — Extraction still stops at the end of the Key Files section: a
  following `#`/`##`/`###` heading or standalone bold section marker terminates
  the list, so prose lines and acceptance-criteria bullets never leak in as
  paths (regression guard for the SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2 defect class).
- **AC5** — A regression test demonstrates the defect before the fix (red on the
  current implementation, green after), and the end-to-end path is verified:
  `implement.py start` on a `## **Key Files:**` item with only unrelated dirty
  paths creates the worktree, leaves the dirty files untouched and records the
  decision in a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — The gate's safety properties are preserved: no
  stash/commit/revert of dirty files, and abort-and-ask still fires for "no Key
  Files section" and for any overlap.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments and docstrings in `implement.py` and the accepted-forms
  list in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree
  gate, SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR) plus the project README and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`** plus its tests and docs
  (producer decision Q2 = A). The two sibling parsers — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — are fixed by linked follow-up
  items (below), not here.
- **The gate stays conservative.** No Key Files section, or any overlapping
  dirty path, must still abort and ask. Nothing here may turn the gate into a
  whitelist or relax "never stash/commit/revert the user's work".
- **Must not regress existing forms.** The new matcher may be more tolerant but
  never stricter: an item that starts cleanly today must still start cleanly.
- **Minimal surface.** No new configuration knob or environment variable.
- **UK English** in comments, docstrings and docs.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` (~line 1671),
  `extract_key_files_from_description()` (~1676),
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files()` (~1712), `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()`
  (~1742), and the `phase_start` call site (~5993) that turns a
  `can_proceed: false` verdict into the dirty-worktree abort.
- The extractor's loop already terminates on a `#`-heading line or a non-bullet
  line starting with `**`; only the initial heading match is wrong. A new
  matcher must not let the matched heading's own bold marker look like the
  section end.
- `skill/implement/tests/` has suites for the start/finish gates but none that
  exercises the Key Files extractor or the relevance classifier.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate
  section) enumerates the three supported forms and needs the tolerant list.

## Desired change

1. Replace the two-branch heading regex with one form-agnostic matcher: an
   optional H1–H6 prefix, an optional `**` bold marker, `Key Files`, an optional
   parenthetical qualifier and optional closing `**`/`:`, matched
   case-insensitively — while still requiring `Key Files` to be the first
   content token (so `## Notes on Key Files` stays unmatched unless it matches
   today).
2. Keep the section terminator and the bullet/backtick path parsing unchanged
   (including `path → note`).
3. Add the table-driven tests (AC1–AC5) and the end-to-end `start` regression.
4. Update the docstring/comment and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — form-agnostic `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE`,
  extractor terminator/docstrings; classifier branches unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_key_files_extraction.py` — new table-driven tests
  for the accepted forms, the terminator behaviour and
  `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` proceed/abort decisions.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — accepted-forms list in the
  Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate section.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — over/under-matching:** tightening "first content token" could make a
  heading that matches today (e.g. `## Key Files and notes`) stop matching.
  Keep the match at least as wide as today; assert the old forms in the table.
- **Risk — terminator drift:** after accepting the new form the loop must not
  treat the matched heading's own `**` as a section end.
- **Risk — untestable "it works now" claims:** the AC5 end-to-end check needs a
  deliberately dirty main checkout, so it must leave the dirty files untouched
  and clean up after itself (or exercise the classifier/`phase_start` seam
  directly).
- **Assumption:** the H2-wrapped form is agent-authored markdown, not framework
  output — so the fix belongs in the tolerant parser, not in the plan skill's
  emitter.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the plan/audit parsers are separate items (below);
  anything further discovered goes to `discovered-from` items, not this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR** — Allow implement.py start to create a clean worktree
  when main checkout is dirty: introduced the gate and the three-form parser;
  this item fixes its blind spot.
- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** — project-local skill extensions / dirty-tree
  exemptions (the other documented relaxation path of the same gate).
- **SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2** — `plan_helpers._parse_key_files_section` did not stop
  at Markdown headings (same failure family: section-boundary parsing).
- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** — generated `standups/` output not gitignored: the
  source of the six dirty files in the reproduction.
- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — the previous framework fix discovered from a
  tce-the-rising implement run (disposition precedent for this re-filing).
- **RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU** — Face-off tie epic whose children carry the
  `## **Key Files:**` form and whose drive run hit the abort.

## Linked follow-up items (producer decision Q2 = B and C)

- **Follow-up 1 — plan parser:** `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  `_parse_key_files_section` / `validate_key_files_format` should accept the same
  heading forms so plan validation does not report a missing/empty Key Files
  section for a validly-written description.
- **Follow-up 2 — audit parser:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`'s Key
  Files extraction (`^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$`) has the same blind spot, which
  omits the item's files from the Phase 2 file-scope manifest. Either fix it
  locally or extract one shared, heading-aware Key Files helper consumed by
  implement/plan/audit.

Both are filed with `discovered-from:<this item>`; their SA ids are recorded in
this item's comments.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

Interview raised on RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (comment `RISE-C0MVWO1N400000N41`),
answered by the producer in-session on 2026-10-31. Answers are transcribed
verbatim.

- **Q1 — Which worklog/store carries the fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A - delete this when filed"** → the fix is re-filed in
  the SorraAgents worklog as this item (with `discovered-from:RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8`)
  and the RISE item is deleted once this item exists. Recommended option A was
  accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 — How wide is the parser fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A, with B and C as linked follow-ups"** →
  `implement.py` only in this item; the plan parser (B) and audit parser (C) are
  filed as linked follow-up items rather than folded in. Recommended option A
  was accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 — Which heading variants must be accepted?**
  **Answer (producer): "B + C"** → accept any `Key Files` heading regardless of
  emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or case (B), **and** tolerate whitespace /
  colon variants of the bare bold marker (C). Recommended option was B; the
  producer widened it to B+C, reflected in AC1/AC2. Source: interactive reply,
  this session.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — Does the framework emit the
  H2-wrapped form?** No: `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py:127-160` and
  `skill/plan/SKILL.md:181,306` specify a bare `**Key Files:**` line; the
  H2-wrapped form in the consumer store was authored into descriptions directly.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — How many items are affected in the
  consumer store?** 9 of 386 (`tce-the-rising`), all inside the face-off tie
  epic. Evidence: SQL scan of that store's `workitems.description`.

# Release gate (merge-dev-to-main.sh) discards the runner JSON, so a dev→main release cannot say why the suite gate failed

Discovered-from: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (during `/skill:plan`).

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` runs the full-suite release
gate as:

```bash
if python3 "$TEST_RUNNER" --scope full --strict-git-env 2>&1; then
```

The runner's machine-readable result is never requested and the exit code is
the only signal, so a slot-contention expiry (`slot_busy`), a killed suite
(`killed`) and a genuine red suite all produce the same message: "Full test
suite failed on the merged dev→main tree — the release is blocked." The
operator cannot tell "fix the code" from "wait for a slot / raise
`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", and a release attempt can burn hours of queue wait before
failing indistinguishably from a real regression.

The pre-push hook gets the equivalent fix under **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (its
AC2/AC3); this item is the same defect on the release path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The release gate consumes the runner's machine-readable result and reports the same `gate_reason=<code>` vocabulary the pre-push hook uses.
- [ ] A slot-contention or killed-run failure prints a distinct message with the remediation hint (wait then re-run, or raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), while a red suite keeps its current message.
- [ ] The gate still fails closed (non-zero exit, no release) in every failure case, and `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` still bypasses it.
- [ ] A hermetic test (following `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py`) pins the classification for slot contention, killed and red-suite cases.

## Notes

- Reuse the shared classifier introduced by SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI rather than a second copy; this item is deliberately **not** a child of it so the release path can ship independently.
- UK English throughout.

## Goal

As a producer/agent, I want a single, reproducible per-test-file **keep / rework / prune** verdict that combines churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime evidence, so test-value decisions are made from one reconciled report rather than four separate reads.

## Problem statement

Today the evidence for test value is fragmented across `skill/test-churn` (evolution/growth), the mutation-testing campaign (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`, fault detection), `evaluate_usefulness.py` + `test-writing-guidelines.md` (static anti-patterns) and the test runner (runtime/flake). Each answers a different question; none produces an auditable per-file verdict. Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` needs a repeatable classify → prove → report pipeline, and this skill is the missing connective tissue between those signals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ingests, per test file: churn metrics (rewrite/growth/stability), mutation score, anti-pattern verdicts, and runtime/flake data when available.
- [ ] Emits one verdict per file — `keep`, `rework` or `prune` — with the evidence for that verdict recorded.
- [ ] Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope, and every verdict cites at least one evidence source.
- [ ] Produces `test_value_report.md` + `test_value_data.json` with documented definitions and limitations.
- [ ] Orchestrates the existing analysers; it does not reimplement churn, mutation or anti-pattern detection.
- [ ] Missing inputs degrade honestly (the report states which signals were absent; it never fabricates a verdict).
- [ ] Reproducible (pinned inputs, documented command, deterministic ordering) and covered by tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the analysed project.
- Must not turn a heuristic into an automatic deletion; `prune` is advisory and conservative.
- No per-project hardcoded paths; project root is an argument.
- Follows the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (classify/prove/report).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (behavioural evidence arm).

## Goal

As a test-value reviewer, I want a cheap static measure of how a test asserts and how much it relies on mocks, so I can pre-filter the suites that mutation testing should examine and give `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-style coupling an enforceable signal.

## Problem statement

`evaluate_usefulness.py` detects only crude anti-patterns (source-grep, placeholder, zero assertions, self-referential). It cannot distinguish a test that asserts observable behaviour from one that asserts internal collaborator calls, nor quantify mock density — yet mock density is a central independent variable in the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults. Without this signal, the mutation campaign has no cheap way to choose where to spend its runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parses TypeScript/JavaScript (and ideally Python) test files and reports per file: assertion count, assertions on internal collaborators vs public behaviour, mock/stub/spy count and ratio, and tests with no meaningful assertion.
- [ ] Flags `toHaveBeenCalledWith`/mock-call assertions on internal collaborators as a distinct, actionable signal (aligned with `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G`).
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with documented definitions and conservative thresholds.
- [ ] Handles dynamic/indirect assertion styles without crashing, and reports uncertainty rather than a false verdict.
- [ ] Runs as a cheap pre-filter (no test execution) and documents that it is a proxy, not ground truth.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Static analysis only; never executes the target project's tests.
- Conservative: uncertainty is reported, never auto-pruned.
- Language-neutral entry point with per-language adapters; no hardcoded project paths.

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — regression test

# Problem statement

The audit runner's default parent-first flow re-screens gap-mapped children on every parent audit run instead of reusing their content-fresh stored audits, and in `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` mode (default `true`) it overwrites previously serviced child audits with stale `partial` reports — making parent audits loop forever when children have been serviced but the parent still carries gaps.

## Users

- **Producer/Agent**: Runs parent audits on epics with terminal children; expects serviced child audits to persist and the parent to converge.
- **Herdr/Downtime workers**: Automate audits; they hit infinite loops and destroy good audit verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Reuse before re-screen.** In the default parent-first flow (`audit_children=False`), when `parent_gaps` is true and a gap-mapped child has a content-fresh stored audit, the parent reuses the child's persisted AC verdicts and does NOT add the child to `pending_children`.
- **AC2 — Serviced audits are never overwritten.** A parent run must never persist a pending-`partial` child report over a child audit that is content-fresh and carries real (non-pending) verdicts.
- **AC3 — Convergence.** After servicing child screens in-main-slot, a parent re-run reports the single unsatisfiable parent AC only (no `Child screens pending` gate) and clears the `<id>.pending-screens.json` signal.
- **AC4 — Regression tests.** Unit tests cover both flows: (a) gap-mapped child reuse skips re-screening, (b) persist does not overwrite a content-fresh serviced child audit. No real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess.

## Impact

Agents running parent audits on epics with serviced children no longer hit infinite re-screen loops or lose their hard-won child audit verdicts — parent audits converge on the first clean pass.

## Constraints

- Must not change the `--audit-children` pre-pass behaviour (it already works correctly).
- In-main-slot mode must remain sequential (no parallelism change).
- Changes must be backwards compatible with existing persisted child audits.

## Existing state

`audit_runner.py::_phase_children` (parent-first `else` branch from ~line 14184; gap-mapped child loop at ~line 14240–14330): when `parent_gaps` is true, the `elif child["id"] in gap_child_ids:` branch (~line 14319) unconditionally appends the child to `pending_children` without checking `_get_child_audit_verdict()` or `_child_content_changed()`. The `--audit-children` pre-pass (same function, `audit_children=True`, ~line 13756) already calls `_get_child_audit_verdict()` and reuses fresh audits. In-main-slot mode then emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens and persists a `partial` child report; a later persist pass overwrites any previously serviced, evidence-backed child audit.

## Desired change

1. **AC1**: In the parent-first gap-mapped path, before adding a child to `pending_children`, consult its stored audit via `_get_child_audit_verdict()` (as the `--audit-children` path does). If content-fresh, adopt the persisted verdicts and skip re-screening.
2. **AC2**: In the persist path for child audits, guard against overwriting a content-fresh child audit. If the target child already has a fresh stored audit with real verdicts, skip persisting the parent-generated pending report.
3. **AC3**: With AC1 + AC2 in place, the `pending-screens.json` signal clears after servicing and the parent converges.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_children` (parent-first gap-mapped child loop ~line 14240–14330; child persist ~line 14438–14475)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_get_child_audit_verdict()` (~line 8182), `_child_content_changed()` (~line 8864)
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — `persist_audit()` (the persistence entry point)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_persist_child_audit()` (~line 7752)
- `skill/audit/tests/` — New/modified tests for gap-mapped reuse and persist-overwrite guards

## Related work

- SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB — the epic whose audit exposed this bug (discovered-from)
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45 / SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3 — unserviced in-main-slot handling (mitigates reporting side only)
- LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X — cross-repo consumer AC that makes the parent permanently partial on this host
- SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F — opt-in child audit cascade with run cap (context)
- SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM — related context (find-related)
- SA-0MU32TE120012T49 — related context (find-related)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions — the root cause, evidence, and acceptance criteria are fully specified in the work item description.

## Problem

`tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (added in v0.1.25) builds a fixture release repo and drives `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` with a stubbed suite runner. Under a clean shell the module is green (verified: `run_tests.py --scope full --force` at tree a9b008ead → 5820 passed). Under the **pre-push hook** (i.e. any push to `dev`/`main`) the same three tests fail:

```
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestGreenGate::test_green_gate_invokes_full_scope_and_release_proceeds
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestRedGate::test_red_gate_blocks_release_before_pr
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestMissingRunnerFailClosed::test_missing_runner_fails_closed
FileNotFoundError: .../runner-marker.txt   (the stubbed runner was never invoked)
```

Root cause: git exports `GIT_DIR` (and the suite gate may export `GIT_INDEX_FILE`) into hook environments; the fixture repo's git commands then resolve against the *live* checkout instead of the fixture, so `merge-dev-to-main.sh` short-circuits and the suite gate never runs. This is the same class as SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX (node fixtures inheriting the finish gate's `GIT_INDEX_FILE`).

**Consequence:** the pre-push full-suite gate is red for every `dev` push, so `dev` cannot be synced with `main` after a release (hit during the 2026-11-02 v0.1.25 release; the sync required `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` with a separately verified green tree).

## Impact

Users can now push `dev` after a release without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, enabling automated `dev`→`main` promotion to complete without manual intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` scrubs the ambient git environment (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` or equivalent) for both the fixture repo construction and the merge-script subprocess, so it passes when run from a git hook.
2. A regression test proves the module passes with `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to the live repository.
3. `git push origin dev` (fast-forward) succeeds without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` after the fix.
4. Full suite green in both a clean shell and a hook-like environment.

## Related

- SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX — same leak class for node fixtures.
- SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42 — audit/producer-review churn (unrelated, same release session).
data.title: tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py is not hermetic: fails under the pre-push hook's exported GIT_DIR, blocking dev pushes

data.description:
## Problem statement

The paid MunitoAI DeepSeek configuration lives only in the tracked
`.pi-config/agent` files and in this machine's `~/.pi/agent/models.json`, because
`scripts/install_pi.sh` merely copies those files **when the destination does not
already exist** — any established machine keeps its own (possibly drifted)
`models.json` and never receives the MunitoAI provider. The newer paid model
`deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is not configured at all, and no
DeepSeek/MunitoAI entry is in `enabledModels`, so paid DeepSeek cannot be reached
from the model cycle.

## Users

Framework operator (producer) on any machine that installs SorraAgents, and any
agent session that wants to run a paid DeepSeek model.

- As an operator, I want `scripts/install_pi.sh` to apply the tracked MunitoAI
  paid-DeepSeek provider to `~/.pi/agent/models.json` even when that file already
  exists, so every project on every machine gets the same model set without me
  hand-editing JSON.
- As an operator, I want the paid DeepSeek models in `enabledModels`, so I can
  reach them with `Ctrl+P` model cycling and as a startup selection.
- As an agent session, I want to select
  `MunitoAI/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` and have it answer, so paid
  DeepSeek is usable for real work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.pi-config/agent/models.json` exposes **both** paid MunitoAI DeepSeek
  models under one `MunitoAI` provider — `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`
  (existing) and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` (new) — with
  `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"`; no credential is committed.
- [ ] `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` `enabledModels` contains `MunitoAI/*` and
  `deepseek/deepseek*` in addition to the existing `Local Proxy/plan` and
  `Local Proxy/code` entries.
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` merges the tracked `providers` (models and
  `modelOverrides` included) into an existing `~/.pi/agent/models.json` and
  unions the tracked `enabledModels` into `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, instead
  of only copying when absent: no interactive prompt is required,
  **local-only providers/models/patterns are preserved**, and the run prints a
  per-provider summary (`Added …` / `OK: already present …`). Proven by an
  install run against a pre-populated sandboxed `$HOME` whose `models.json`
  lacks `MunitoAI` (today that run prints `Skipped …/models.json` and installs
  nothing).
- [ ] The merge is idempotent and non-destructive: a second run leaves both files
  semantically unchanged (no duplicated models, no lost local entries), a single
  timestamped `models.json.bak.<ts>` / `settings.json.bak.<ts>` backup is written
  before the first modification, writes are atomic (temp file + rename), and an
  unparseable existing JSON is reported and left untouched (fail-open, never
  half-written or overwritten).
- [ ] Post-install verification succeeds on a machine holding a valid MunitoAI
  credential: `pi --list-models munito` lists both MunitoAI DeepSeek models and
  `pi -p --no-tools --model MunitoAI/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017
  "reply with ok"` returns a response.
- [ ] Tests cover the merge helper and the install wiring (fresh install,
  pre-existing drifted file, idempotent re-run, local-only provider preserved,
  malformed JSON fail-safe) using a sandboxed `$HOME`; the new tests fail before
  the change and pass after it.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No credentials in the repository: keep `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"` env
  interpolation. The operator's stored `auth.json` credential (present on this
  machine) takes precedence over that env var at runtime.
- The merge must be non-destructive: it may add or refresh tracked providers, but
  must never drop a locally defined provider, model, `modelOverrides` entry or
  `enabledModels` pattern; write atomically (temp file + rename).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` must stay non-interactive-safe — the test harness runs
  it with `stdin=/dev/null`, where the current prompt degrades to `Skipped`.
- Keep existing install conventions: idempotent helpers, `create_symlink`
  backup-not-delete behaviour, fail-open warnings, `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL`
  opt-out unaffected.
- MunitoAI publishes no context/pricing metadata (`GET /inference/v1/models`
  returns ids only), so `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` for the new model mirror the
  existing `…v4-flash` entry (400000 / 16384) and must be flagged as unverified
  in a code comment.
- Do not widen scope to other MunitoAI models (`zai-org/glm-5.3-flash`,
  `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, `munito/ocr-*`, …) — record them as follow-up work items if
  they become interesting.

## Existing state

- `.pi-config/agent/models.json` already contains a `MunitoAI` provider
  (`https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1`, `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"`) with a
  single model `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` ("MunitoAI DeepSeek V4 Flash
  (paid)", 400000 / 16384, `input: ["text"]`). It arrived incidentally in
  `1ea3f20d3` ("chore: commit pre-existing working-tree leftovers before
  release"), untracked by any work item.
- `~/.pi/agent/models.json` on this machine is byte-identical to the tracked
  file and `pi --list-models munito` already lists
  `MunitoAI deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`.
- `GET https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1/models` (queried with the stored
  credential) returns 11 ids, two of them DeepSeek:
  `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`.
  A live non-streaming call to `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` returned
  HTTP 200 with content `ok` plus a `reasoning` field.
- `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` (and the installed copy) has
  `enabledModels: ["Local Proxy/plan", "Local Proxy/code"]` — no DeepSeek or
  MunitoAI entry.
- **The install gap:** `scripts/install_pi.sh` uses
  `copy_if_missing_or_prompt` for `settings.json`/`models.json`. Reproduced
  against a sandboxed `$HOME` holding a pre-existing `models.json` without
  `MunitoAI`: the run prints `Skipped …/models.json` and the resulting file has
  no `MunitoAI` provider.
- `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` already holds a `MunitoAI` key (52 chars);
  `$MUNITOAI_API_KEY` is not set in the environment.

## Desired change

1. Add `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` to the tracked `MunitoAI` provider
   in `.pi-config/agent/models.json`, keeping the existing `…v4-flash` entry.
2. Add `MunitoAI/*` and `deepseek/deepseek*` to the tracked `enabledModels`.
3. Replace the consent-only whole-file copy in `scripts/install_pi.sh` with an
   idempotent, non-interactive **merge** of the tracked `providers` into
   `~/.pi/agent/models.json` plus a union merge of `enabledModels` into
   `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`; keep whole-file copy only for a missing
   destination. Back up before the first modification, write atomically, and fail
   open (warn, leave the file intact) on unparseable JSON.
4. Document the behaviour and the post-install verification commands.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi-config/agent/models.json` — add the `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
  entry to the existing `MunitoAI` provider block.
- `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` — extend `enabledModels` with `MunitoAI/*` and
  `deepseek/deepseek*`.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — replace `copy_if_missing_or_prompt` usage for
  `models.json`/`settings.json` with the merge step (keeping copy-if-missing for a
  fresh `$HOME`).
- `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` (new) — dependency-free (stdlib) idempotent
  JSON merge helper: provider/model refresh, `enabledModels` union, atomic write,
  timestamped backup, fail-open on invalid JSON; invoked by `install_pi.sh`.
- `tests/test_install_pi_models_config.py` (new) — sandboxed-`$HOME` install
  wiring: fresh install, pre-populated drifted config gains `MunitoAI`,
  local-only provider preserved, idempotent re-run, malformed JSON fail-safe.
- `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py` (new) — unit tests for merge semantics,
  backup creation, atomicity, `enabledModels` union.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — document the global install's config merge
  behaviour and post-install verification (`pi --list-models munito`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** tracked values win for providers the tracked config defines
  (including a locally customised `MunitoAI` block); every *other* local
  provider/model/override is untouched.
- **Assumption (OPEN QUESTION):** `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is
  included because it is the newer paid DeepSeek model on the account; the
  operator's Q1 answer focused on installation and did not explicitly name it.
  Dropping it is a one-line revert.
- **Assumption:** `…v4.1-flash-1017` shares the existing `…v4-flash` limits
  (400000 / 16384). Unverified — MunitoAI publishes no metadata; a wrong value
  only mis-sizes pi's context accounting.
- **Risk (thinking metadata):** the new model returns a `reasoning` field, but
  whether the endpoint accepts reasoning-effort parameters is unverified;
  do not set `reasoning: true`/`thinkingFormat` without a streaming probe. Start
  by mirroring the existing entry; record a follow-up if tuning is needed.
- **Risk (local config clobbering):** a naive merge could drop an operator's
  bespoke provider or `modelOverrides`. Mitigation: preserve unknown providers
  verbatim, back up first, atomic rename, explicit test for the
  local-only-provider case.
- **Risk (auth mismatch):** `auth.json` wins over `$MUNITOAI_API_KEY`; a machine
  with neither sees the model as unavailable. Mitigation: keep the existing
  `pi login` reminder.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other MunitoAI models (GLM, Qwen, OCR) and DeepSeek
  provider tuning are tempting to bundle. Mitigation: out of scope; capture as
  linked follow-up items.
- **Risk (framework-wide blast radius):** every project runs
  `install_pi.sh`; a merge bug could corrupt `~/.pi/agent` config widely.
  Mitigation: fail-open on unparseable JSON, backup, atomic write, stdlib-only
  helper.

## Related work

- **SA-0MO4PG0U5004UJGP** — Add tracked .pi config and improve install_pi.sh to
  prompt for pi login (introduced the copy-if-missing/prompt install this item
  amends).
- **SA-0MQZXFKA9007FKU4** — Update pi-agent config: Local Proxy provider, model
  updates, version bump (precedent for editing tracked model config).
- **SA-0MTT7EUH30054I41** — Disable Pi auto-compaction for Local Proxy/plan
  (precedent for tracked `.pi-config/agent` changes with tests).
- Commits: `ebc5a1d7d` ("Add Deepseek" — direct DeepSeek provider),
  `1ea3f20d3` (introduced the `MunitoAI` provider block incidentally).
- **SA-0MW0GL4590046BTK** (this item).

### Automated find-related report

Generated by `/skill:find-related` (keyword-based, low signal here — the manual
list above is authoritative):

- **SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63** – Remote dev branch corrupted by test fixtures (test
  isolation bug) (completed)
- **SA-0MQZZ93110003MBU** – Add review of affected files in plan review stages
  (completed)
- **SA-0MUQ0I0YY000JCB5** – Remove stale references to missing .ralph.json and
  ralph config system (completed)
- Repository file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `standups/2026_09_26.md` (keyword
  overlap only; not substantively related).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which MunitoAI deepseek model(s) should the config expose — (a) add
  `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` alongside the existing `…v4-flash`,
  (b) replace `…v4-flash`, (c) other?" — Answer (Map, interactive reply): "I see
  that we have a configuration in the local pi config. I want that config
  available to all projects using SorraAgents, the `./scripts/install_pi.sh`
  script should add it." → reframed the item: the tracked MunitoAI paid-DeepSeek
  config must be installed for every project/machine by `scripts/install_pi.sh`,
  not merely exist in the tracked file. Research: reproduced that
  `install_pi.sh` prints `Skipped …/models.json` when the destination already
  exists (sandboxed `$HOME`), so tracked config never lands on established
  machines.
- Q2: "Should the model be scoped into `enabledModels`? (a) add patterns,
  (b) leave untouched." — Answer (Map, interactive reply): "a - also add the
  `deepseek/deepseek*` model to `enabledModels`." → add `MunitoAI/*` **and**
  `deepseek/deepseek*` to the tracked `enabledModels`.
- Q3: "Does this work include applying the config locally and verifying it?" —
  Answer (Map, interactive reply): "see 1" → yes; installing via
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` and verifying selection/execution is in scope, hence
  the merge behaviour is an acceptance criterion.
- Q4 (agent research, no operator input needed): "Which DeepSeek ids does
  MunitoAI actually serve?" — Answer: `GET /inference/v1/models` with the stored
  credential returns `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` and
  `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`; a live call to the latter returned
  HTTP 200 (`content: "ok"`, plus `reasoning`).
- **OPEN QUESTION:** should `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` be added, or
  is `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` alone sufficient? Default taken: add both
  (newer paid model, additive, one-line revert). Context: operator's Q1 answer
  did not name the model explicitly.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-07: Plan decomposition complete (plan skill). 8 child work items created in test-first dependency order. AC coverage: 100% (`tree_coverage` recommendation: `proceed`). Key Files validated.
  1. **Update tracked models.json** (SA-0MW6RY8O1006M3F2) — add `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` to the MunitoAI provider.
  2. **Update tracked settings.json** (SA-0MW6RZ3AO0074UK6) — add `MunitoAI/*` and `deepseek/deepseek*` to `enabledModels`.
  3. **Unit tests for merge helper** (SA-0MW6S2MAL004U5KX) — test-first; no dependencies.
  4. **Create merge helper** (SA-0MW6S07QM005C6U2) — depends on the unit tests.
  5. **Integration tests for install wiring** (SA-0MW6S4NAQ001MAM1) — depends on merge helper and both data changes.
  6. **Update install_pi.sh** (SA-0MW6S1SEU005IDJ6) — depends on merge helper and integration tests.
  7. **Documentation** (SA-0MW6S4OSG008PYL1) — depends on merge helper and install script.
  8. **Verify post-install availability** (SA-0MW6SDDWD0008211) — depends on install script and both data changes.

## Plan: resolved ambiguities

- **"Flagged as unverified in a code comment"** — `models.json` is JSON and cannot carry comments. The unverified `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` flag for `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is recorded in the merge helper's docstring/constants (`scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py`) and in `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`. Resolution recorded in child SA-0MW6RY8O1006M3F2. If an in-file marker is required, a non-standard `//` comment would invalidate the JSON and is rejected.
- **OPEN QUESTION (carried forward): should `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` be added?** Default taken: add both models (newer paid model, purely additive, one-line revert if unwanted). Not blocking — implementation proceeds with the default; flagged here for producer awareness.

# `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's non-initialised `.worklog` (and can build `.worklog/.worklog`)

> **Provenance:** `discovered-from:SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (which was transferred
> from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT`, itself `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`).
> Filed separately by producer decision so the parent fix stays narrow.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/code_freeze.py` carries its **own** copy of
`_detect_worklog_dir()`. It builds ancestor candidates as `parent / ".worklog"`
for every parent and accepts any `.worklog` directory without checking that it
is initialised. Consequences:

- from a linked worktree root whose committed `.worklog/` holds only
  `config.yaml`, `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
  `<worktree>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` — a marker file that can never exist,
  so the fail-closed freeze gate silently sees "no freeze";
- from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no committed `.worklog`), a
  stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory would be selected, giving
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

The correct marker in both cases is `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

## Users

- **AI agent running `/skill:implement` from a worktree** — the implement
  workflow consults the code-freeze marker; reading the wrong path makes the
  freeze gate miss an active freeze.
  Story: *As an implementing agent in a worktree, an active code freeze must be
  detected, so I stop instead of landing a commit that the freeze forbids.*
- **Producer/operator** — an activated freeze must be effective immediately for
  every checkout.
  Story: *As the producer, when I activate a freeze, agents working in
  worktrees must observe it without extra `--worklog-dir` instructions.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs one resolution rule, not two divergent copies.
  Story: *As a maintainer, code-freeze marker resolution must not silently drift
  from `status_lifecycle`'s worklog-dir rule.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves the main marker.** With cwd at a linked
      worktree root that has a committed, **uninitialised** `.worklog/`
      (`config.yaml` only), `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.
- [ ] **AC2 — no `.worklog/.worklog` nesting.** With cwd inside
      `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, the marker path is
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` even when a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC3 — explicit `project_root` unchanged.** `code_freeze_marker_path(<root>)`
      still returns `<root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` and is unaffected by the
      cwd-based rule.
- [ ] **AC4 — one rule, not two.** `code_freeze._detect_worklog_dir()` either
      re-uses the shared resolution helper from `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
      (preferred — no duplicated walk) or mirrors it exactly, with a comment
      naming the shared rule as authoritative.
- [ ] **AC5 — unit tests.** Hermetic `tmp_path` tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` for AC1–AC3 (no real
      `git worktree`, no network), alongside the existing marker tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The `code_freeze.py` docstrings state the
      initialised-only / no-nesting rule; if resolution is shared, note it in
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` next to the `StatusLifecycle` note.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not widen the freeze semantics: this is a path-resolution fix, not a
  change to how a freeze is activated, cleared, or enforced.
- Keep the existing public API (`code_freeze_marker_path`, marker read/write
  helpers) and their `project_root` behaviour unchanged.
- Prefer re-using the shared helper over a second walk; if that would create a
  circular import, mirror the rule and reference the canonical one in a
  comment.
- Gate order: build → test → commit; no ad-hoc `pytest` — run tests through the
  test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake of the parent item)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 48) order:
  explicit `project_root` → `<cwd>/.worklog` → `<git toplevel>/.worklog` →
  `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`, each gated on `is_dir()` only.
- `code_freeze_marker_path()` (~line 90) uses that helper and falls back to
  `<cwd>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` when nothing resolves.
- The same candidate-construction defect is proven in
  `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` (parent item
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB`, AC1–AC3) — this item is the same rule applied to the
  code-freeze copy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` / marker path
  resolution (~lines 48–101).
- `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` — new worktree-layout cases

## Problem statement

The audit pipeline currently treats *any* failing test as a failure of the audit: a red F3 auto-execution leaves execution-dependent ACs `partial` (so `Ready to close: No`), and a red merge-gate suite run fails the integration closed. That is the right behaviour for the release gate, but it is wrong for the everyday audits an agent runs while implementing a work item: unrelated, pre-existing red unit tests (e.g. another item's broken test) block an otherwise complete item and send the audit into a remediation loop that cannot succeed.

Audits must therefore support two test-failure modes: **strict** (today's behaviour — any failing test fails the audit) and **permissive** (a failing **unit** test that is provably *not affected in any way* by the audited work item's changes does not fail the audit; integration/end-to-end failures always fail).

## Users

- **Agent implementing a work item** — "As an agent running `/skill:audit` on my in-progress item, I want an unrelated red unit test elsewhere in the repo not to block my item, so that I do not chase failures outside my change set."
- **Release engineer (ship skill)** — "As the release gate, I want every audited item to have a genuinely green suite, so that `dev` is never promoted to `main` on the back of excused failures."
- **Producer reviewing an audit** — "As a reviewer, I want the persisted audit report to state which mode was used and, for every excused failure, the evidence that it was unrelated, so that I can trust a permissive pass."

Example user stories:

- Permissive: `tests/test_other_skill.py::test_unrelated` fails; the item only touched `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`; the audit still returns `Ready to close: Yes` with the failure listed as excused (unrelated, unit) and a critical `test-failure` work item created.
- Strict: the same failure blocks the audit; ship re-runs the item under `--strict` and refuses to release.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mode resolution and default.** `audit_runner.py issue` (and `batch`) accepts `--strict` / `--no-strict`, with `AUDIT_STRICT=1` as the environment equivalent; **the default is permissive**. Precedence is flag > env > default, resolved once and recorded. Unit tests cover the precedence matrix and that `--strict` reproduces today's verdict for a red suite (any failure ⇒ `Ready to close: No`).
2. **Permissive excusal — unrelated unit failures.** In permissive mode, a red suite whose failures are **all** unit-classified **and** proven unrelated to the item's changes does not fail the audit: the runner injects a "run red, excused failures" evidence block into the Phase 1/Phase 2 prompts (so execution-dependent ACs may be marked `met`), the report gains a `## Test Failure Mode` section listing every excused failure with its classification and relatedness evidence, and the `--json` payload carries the same data. Unit tests cover the excused path end-to-end at the verdict level.
3. **Permissive fail-closed cases.** In permissive mode the audit still fails when (a) any failure is integration/end-to-end classified, (b) any unit failure is affected by the item's changes, or (c) relatedness is inconclusive and no baseline comparison can be performed. Unit tests cover each case individually, plus the mixed case (one excusable + one blocking failure ⇒ audit fails).
4. **Scope classification and relatedness algorithm.** Failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.
5. **Triage is preserved.** Excused failures are still triaged into critical `test-failure` work items (same dedup + cap semantics as today). Unit tests assert triage is invoked for excused failures as well as blocking ones.
6. **Ship uses strict mode.** All three ship audit call sites (`check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`, `refresh-audits.js`) pass `--strict`, and the manual remediation commands they surface include `--strict`. Tests assert the constructed command strings; the flag name is generic (`--strict`, not `--strict-tests`) so future strictness checks can share it.
7. **Freshness respects mode strength.** A strict run must never reuse a stored permissive "Yes" (it re-runs); a permissive run may reuse a stored strict "Yes". Unit tests cover both directions.
8. **Documentation and validation.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document both modes, the flag/env precedence, the classification and relatedness rules, and which callers use which mode. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only mandate:** the audit stays read-only except for the existing sanctioned exceptions. The baseline comparison runs only the failing tests, in a scratch worktree (never the main checkout), through the existing paced runner (`run_tests.paced_runner()`) and under the existing `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down so nested suite runs cannot recurse.
- **Strict mode must be byte-for-byte today's behaviour** — no verdict change for existing strict callers.
- **Never-block guarantee (F4) is preserved:** the mode never introduces a hard exit for infrastructure failure; inability to classify or baseline degrades to *affected* (fail closed on the verdict), never a crash.
- **The dev-push pre-push full-suite gate is unchanged** — permissive mode does not weaken it; it only governs the audit verdict.
- **Determinism:** the excusal decision must be reproducible from the persisted report alone (mode, classification, mapping/baseline evidence recorded).
- **No new suite executions on the happy path:** a green suite behaves exactly as today; excusal work happens only when the suite is red.
- Scope-creep guard: any richer relatedness heuristic (e.g. coverage-based mapping), or per-repo `unitTestGlobs`/`integrationTestGlobs` configuration, is out of scope — record it as a linked follow-up if it turns out to be needed.

## Existing state

- `_run_tests_via_test_skill()` (F3 auto-execution) parses failures, triages them, and returns `success`; a red run injects **no** GREEN-RUN block, so execution-dependent ACs stay `partial` ⇒ `Ready to close: No`. Red cached entries (`_classify_full_suite_cache` → `red`) also stay partial with no execution.
- `_integrate_into_dev()` (Phase 1 merge gate) runs `run_suite("all")`; `success == False` ⇒ `Integration failed: test suite failed.` ⇒ audit fails closed.
- Green evidence reaches the parent Phase-1 screen, both child Phase-1 screens and every Phase 2 prompt (`_green_run_prompt_block`, `_auto_green_run_prompt_block`, `_test_skill_run_prompt_block`).
- The freshness gate fingerprints `{title_hash, description_hash}` only — it has no notion of *how* a verdict was produced, so a permissive "Yes" would currently satisfy ship's strict re-run.
- Item changed-file resolution already exists (`_resolve_touched_files`, `_extract_key_files`); failure parsing exists (`parse_pytest_failures`, `parse_node_failures`); suite resolution exists (`full_suite_commands`).
- Ship invokes the runner from `check-audit-gate.js:841`, `check-final-validation.js:479`, `refresh-audits.js:131` (`runAuditCommand` defaults), plus the surfaced manual commands in `check-audit-gate.js:386/518/638` and `audit-remediation.js:43`.
- `pytest.ini` declares only `smoke`/`critical`/`benchmark` markers; the repo has no `integration`/`e2e` markers, and `tests/integration/*.mjs` exists — path convention is the practical classifier.

## Desired change

**Headline:** add a `--strict` audit mode (permissive by default) in which only *unrelated unit* failures are excused, and make the ship release gate audit strictly.

1. **Mode plumbing.** New `--strict` / `--no-strict` flags on `issue` and `batch`, `AUDIT_STRICT` env var, default permissive; a resolved `strict: bool` on `_AuditContext`, threaded to the F3 path, the merge gate, the prompt evidence builders, the report assembler and the `--json` payload.
2. **Failure classification + relatedness module** (helpers in `audit_runner.py`):
   - `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` → `"unit"` | `"integration"` from the path-pattern table (fail closed to `integration`).
   - `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` → `"affected"` | `"unrelated"` | `"inconclusive"` (test file match, import scan against changed modules, shared test-infrastructure match).
   - `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` → per-failure verdicts by re-running only the inconclusive failures in a scratch worktree at the pre-change commit.
3. **Verdict integration.** A single helper (e.g. `_evaluate_red_suite(...)`) that, in strict mode, returns "blocked" for any failure, and in permissive mode returns `blocked` (with reasons) or `excused` (with per-failure evidence). Both the F3 path and the merge gate consume it. Excused-red injects an evidence block analogous to the GREEN-RUN blocks; blocked-red keeps today's behaviour and diagnostics.
4. **Cached-red handling (consistency).** In permissive mode a `red` cached full-suite entry is classified from the cached output (already stored) rather than being accepted as blocking-by-default; if the cached output yields no parseable failure records the runner executes the suite as it does on a miss. Strict mode keeps today's cached-red behaviour unchanged.
5. **Persistence and report.** `## Test Failure Mode` section (mode, resolution source, per-failure classification/relatedness/evidence, baseline commit used); `--json` payload key `test_failure_mode`; the mode is part of the stored audit so the freshness gate can compare mode strength (strict re-runs over permissive; permissive may reuse strict).
6. **Ship wiring.** `--strict` added to the three ship runner invocations and the surfaced manual remediation commands.
7. **Docs.** Audit + ship SKILL files and their `docs/dev/*-reference.md` companions updated with the contract, the default, and the caller matrix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — mode resolution/plumbing; `_classify_test_failure_scope`, `_failure_relatedness`, `_baseline_unrelated`, `_evaluate_red_suite`; excused-red evidence block; `_run_tests_via_test_skill` and `_integrate_into_dev` integration; report + `--json` sections; freshness mode-strength comparison.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — document both modes, the `--strict`/`AUDIT_STRICT` precedence, default, classification/relatedness rules, caller matrix.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — full contract: pattern table, relatedness algorithm, baseline worktree rules, cached-red behaviour, mode-strength freshness.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `runAuditCommand` default + surfaced manual commands gain `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — `runAuditCommand` default gains `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — pre-flight refresh `runAuditCommand` gains `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — state that ship audits strictly.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_strict_mode.py` (new) — mode precedence, classification table, relatedness mapping, baseline comparison, excused/blocked verdicts, triage-on-excusal, cached-red behaviour, freshness mode strength.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — extend existing F3/merge-gate coverage for the strict path parity.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_audit_strict_flag.mjs` (new) — command-string assertions for the three ship call sites.
- `command/audit.md` — note that the default is permissive and `--strict` is available (optional, if the prompt enumerates flags).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: excusal hides a real regression.** Mitigated by fail-closed defaults (integration always fails; affected or inconclusive always fails) and by recording per-failure evidence in the persisted report.
- **Risk: baseline worktree cost/instability** (merge-base unresolvable, worktree add failure, test absent at baseline). Mitigated: baseline runs only the inconclusive failures, and any baseline failure ⇒ treated as affected (fail closed) with the reason recorded.
- **Risk: a permissive "Yes" leaks into the release.** Mitigated by AC6 (ship passes `--strict`) and AC7 (strict never reuses a permissive verdict).
- **Risk: recursion/concurrency** — the baseline run must reuse `paced_runner()` and honour `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`; tests must mock subprocess execution (per the shared test-writing guidelines: no real suite, no real `audit_runner.py issue` child).
- **Assumption:** "integration/end-to-end" is identified by path convention in this repo (no markers exist); richer classification (markers, per-repo globs) is a follow-up if needed.
- **Assumption:** excused failures still create critical `test-failure` items (triage behaviour unchanged).
- **Assumption:** the merge gate proceeds with integration in permissive mode when the only failures are excused, recording them in the merge-gate evidence (strict keeps failing closed).
- **Assumption:** `--strict` is a generic audit-strictness flag; future strictness checks may join it, so the flag is not named after tests.

## Related work

### Related work items

- **SA-0MSAAUJ1F0026BMN** – Create 'test' skill: run tests, triage failures, validate & fix test usefulness (completed) — the suite execution/triage machinery this change consumes (`run_tests.py`, `parse_pytest_failures`, `check_or_create`).
- **SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG** – Release-gate fail-fast on repository-override vars (completed) — precedent for the release gate taking the conservative path while other callers stay convenient.
- **SA-0MPFD4T0F004RI8I** – CI: Add end-to-end packaging/installation verification for packages/tui (completed) — the end-to-end tests that must never be excused.
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP** – F3 default auto-execution on cache miss (referenced throughout `skill/audit/SKILL.md`; the item is not present in this store) — the path whose red result becomes mode-dependent here.
- **SA-0MT456M27001LRTL** – Phase 1 merge gate (referenced throughout `skill/audit/SKILL.md`; the item is not present in this store) — the second red-suite path in scope.
- **SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP** – Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line (completed) — the freshness gate extended here with mode strength.
- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** – Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits (open) — touches the same audit-runner verdict/lifecycle surface; check for conflicts when implementing.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** – Audit accepts gate-produced full-suite evidence (completed) — the read-only green-evidence path that permissive mode must not weaken.

### Repository file matches

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the pipeline being extended.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — audit contract documentation.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — suite execution, cache scope and triage semantics consumed by the audit.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (mode switch location):** strict default + `--permissive-tests` opt-in / **permissive default + `--strict` in ship** / env-var only. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **b** — permissive is the default and ship passes the strict flag; the flag is named **`--strict`** (not `--strict-tests`) so future strictness requirements can share it. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 (relatedness test):** deterministic path+import mapping / merge-base baseline re-run / **hybrid**. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **c** — deterministic mapping decides the clear cases; only inconclusive failures get the baseline re-run. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 (unit vs integration classification):** **path convention** / pytest markers / configurable globs in `.pi/test-config.json`. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **a** — path convention. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research: `pytest.ini` declares only `smoke`/`critical`/`benchmark` markers, so marker-based classification has no data to work with today; `tests/integration/*.mjs` exists and is matched by the convention.
- **Assumptions put to the producer (no objection recorded):** excused failures are still triaged into critical `test-failure` items and recorded in the report; the mode applies to both the F3 auto-execution and the merge-gate suite paths; the mode and its basis are surfaced in the persisted report and the `--json` payload.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-07 (plan skill)** — Decomposed `SA-0MW0JJ36Z000AF57` into 22 child items (9 test-first tasks, 8 feature slices, 5 auto-created AC-coverage gap items).
  - Effort/risk pre-check: `decision=plan` (Medium effort, Medium risk at intake).
  - Plan-approval gate: `request_approval=false` — no approval pause required (not Extra Large AND High/Severe).
  - AC coverage review: first pass `stop` on 3 weak fuzzy matches; strengthened child ACs for parent ACs 3, 4 and 6; second pass `auto_close` created 5 covering children and advanced stage to `plan_complete`.
  - Dependency graph wired (test-first; feature slices in dependency order): mode plumbing → classification/relatedness → verdict integration → {triage, cached-red, freshness} → ship wiring → docs/full-suite.
  - Effort/risk re-estimate (post-decomposition): Small effort (~8.29h recommended), Medium risk (9/25), 92% confidence.
  - Idempotent: re-running plan reuses existing children (title-matched `wl create` de-duplicates).

## Appendix: Plan interview

No new questions were required in this planning session — all three intake questions (Q1 mode switch, Q2 relatedness test, Q3 classification) were already answered by the producer and recorded in the intake Appendix above. The plan was derived from the intake brief, the recorded answers, and the existing `audit_runner.py` / ship wiring reviewed at planning time.

## Goal

Investigate, and then reduce, large tool-call results before they enter conversation history, so that a single oversized tool result does not inflate every subsequent model turn. Prefer the cheapest effective mechanism; a small-model compaction call is one candidate among several.

## Evidence (from the proxy incident 2026-11-03, LLM repo)

- A single tool-role message of 51,945 bytes (a full SKILL.md pasted into history by the audit skill) entered the conversation at 08:41:54. The conversation grew from 22 KB to 120 KB of content over 7 turns, and the prompt went 6,564 to 33,570 tokens.
- Every subsequent turn re-prefilled the growing tail on a local model measuring 143-303 tok/s prefill, producing 53 s and 72 s time-to-first-byte.
- The proxy priced that 51,945-byte append at 173 new tokens against a measured 12,936 (deficit_ratio 0.659), so the cost was invisible to admission control as well as to the agent.
- Session recordings and session jsonl files are available for measurement: ~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/ and ~/.pi/agent/sessions/.

## Candidate approaches, cheapest first

1. Measure first: rank tool results by bytes/tokens across recorded sessions to identify which tools dominate (skill-body pastes, wl show --json dumps, file reads). Deterministic script, no model call.
2. Truncate with re-read: a Pi extension intercepts a tool result above a threshold, keeps head and tail plus an explicit "truncated N bytes, re-read with offset/limit" marker, and preserves the raw output on disk.
3. Reference instead of inline: content-address large or repeated payloads (skill bodies, already-read files) and substitute a short handle plus preview when the content is already in the prompt.
4. Small-model compaction at the boundary: the extension detects an oversized tool result and asks a small/fast model to compact only what the current request needs, prefixing the tool output with a purpose-built instruction. Must reuse the existing summariser slot (Qwen2.5-7B preset, parallel=1, as pinned by the proxy compaction_summarizer) so it does not contend with the main model, and must only escalate here when approaches 2 and 3 are insufficient, since it is a model call on the critical path.
5. Structured projections at the tool level: JSON field selection, summary-by-default with details on demand, and flags that keep payloads small at source.

## Constraints

- Compaction must be cheaper than the prefill it avoids. Measured saving: avoiding 13k prefill tokens saves roughly 45-90 s at observed rates, so a ~2 s small-model call is a clear win; the strategy must be justified against that budget.
- It must not lose information the agent later needs, and any lossy step must be recoverable (raw payload retained and re-readable).
- It runs on the same GPU as the workload it protects, so it competes for capacity -- another reason to prefer non-model approaches first.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A measurement report exists ranking tool-result payload size by tool and session, produced by a committed deterministic script (no model calls), with the top offenders named.
- AC2: Each of the five candidate approaches is assessed for (a) bytes/tokens saved, (b) added latency and GPU contention, (c) information-loss risk and recoverability, with a recorded recommendation.
- AC3: At least one non-model mechanism (truncate-with-re-read or reference-instead-of-inline) is prototyped as a Pi extension and validated against a real oversized tool result, with the before/after prompt-token counts recorded.
- AC4: If a small-model compaction path is implemented, it reuses the existing summariser slot, is benchmarked against the prefill cost it avoids, and includes a documented fallback when the summariser is unavailable.
- AC5: Documentation states the extension's threshold, behaviour and how an agent recovers truncated content, and the result is recorded against the originating LLM-repo prefill-pricing item.
data.title: Reduce large tool-call results before they enter conversation history
