# Intake brief — implement finish changed-scope gate: prove scoped selection, document order, measure wall clock

**Migrated from AI_Hell `AH-0MVWJYIB4006PZTU`** (producer decision, 2026-11-03): the
subject is `implement.py` / `run_tests.py` gate behaviour, i.e. agent
infrastructure, so it belongs in the framework repository (SorraAgents), not in
the AI_Hell game repo. The AI_Hell item is deleted after this item was created.
Every measurement in the brief below was taken in **`/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell`**
(a Vitest/TypeScript game repo) — that repo is the *case study and measurement
subject*, not the implementation home.

**Mapping of repo-dependent references in the migrated text**

- "this repository" / "this Vitest repo" → **AI_Hell** (`/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell`),
  the consumer repo used for the real-gate evidence and the wall-clock sample.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (AC5) → that page lives in **AI_Hell** and remains
  the owner of the measurement contract; the SorraAgents-side reference for gate
  behaviour is `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.
- **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO** — the framework item named throughout as the selector
  owner — has since been **completed (`done`, shipped in v0.1.25)**, and the
  installed skills already contain the vitest/TS mapping and the
  `suiteCommands`-no-longer-disables-selection fix. It stays referenced here as
  the provenance of the landed fix and of the residual-gap research (cross-ref
  comment `SA-C0MVXW2CB8003BXPJ`).
- Constraint Q3 (a) "no edits to `~/.pi/agent/skills/**` from this repo" is now
  **superseded**: this item lives in the repo that *owns* `skill/`, so the
  proof-and-document work may touch `skill/` if a defect is found — the default
  remains "verify and document, do not re-open selector scope" (Q2 = d).

---

# Intake brief — implement finish changed-scope gate always falls back to the full suite

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** chore (process/tooling; no gameplay behaviour change) ·
**Status:** CONFIRMED — producer answered Q1 (a), Q2 "as recommended" (= d), Q3 (a) on 2026-11-01.

**Decision (producer, 2026-11-01):** *verify-and-narrow*. The filed premise no
longer reproduces against the installed skills; this item now proves the scoped
gate works in a real `implement.py finish`, documents the node/vitest selection
order, and records the wall-clock measurement. Residual selector gaps are
**out of scope here** and filed on framework item **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO**
(comment `SA-C0MVXW2CB8003BXPJ`); no agent-infrastructure edits from this repo.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` is documented to validate **changed scope only** for fast
iteration, but at filing time every finish gate in this repository logged
`changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope` and then ran
the full Vitest suite (≈ 346–409 s loaded, plus host-wide test-slot queueing).

Read-only verification during intake shows the **skill-level fix landed after
this item was filed** and the fallback no longer reproduces: the installed
selector maps vitest `.test.ts`/`.spec.ts` files and picks a subset for every one
of the last 25 commits. What has *not* happened is proof in a real gate (no
finish gate has run since the install), plus documentation and a measurement.
This item delivers exactly that proof.

## Users (user stories)

- *As an implementing agent*, I want `implement.py finish` on a single-file
  change to run only the affected tests, so the build → test → commit loop
  completes in minutes rather than queueing 1–2 h for a full-suite slot.
- *As a producer*, I want the changed-scope gate to still fail on a
  deliberately broken affected test, and the full suite to remain the
  `dev`-push gate, so speed never weakens correctness.
- *As a maintainer of this repo*, I want the node/vitest selection order
  documented so the behaviour is predictable and diagnosable.

## Existing state (verified 2026-11-01, read-only)

### The observed warning no longer exists in the installed skill

The filed log line —

```
WARNING: Implement run_tests: changed-scope selection unavailable in <worktree>
(no dev baseline, no changed tests, custom suiteCommands, or node-only selection)
```

— is the *old* generic message. All five matching logs under `.worklog/tmp/`
(2026-10-31 05:50 → 22:35) contain exactly that text. The installed message is
now specific:
`changed-scope selection unavailable in <path> (<specific reason>)`.

### The changed-scope chain has since been reworked

- `implement.py` `_run_resolved_suite` → `_run_group_from_changed_files` →
  `_run_changed_scope_selection` (shared `run_tests.changed_scope_selection`)
  → full suite. The pytest-only `_run_changed_scope_pytest` path described in
  the original root cause is no longer the general path.
- `run_tests.py` now (a) recognises `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` / `.js` / `.tsx`
  test files in `map_changed_to_tests`, (b) emits
  `node_modules/.bin/vitest run <files>` when the repo uses Vitest, and
  (c) no longer lets `suiteCommands` disable selection (it describes the full
  suite only). Docstrings cite **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO**; the fix was committed

## Migrated from AH-0MVXVADEL005XNWM (AI_Hell worklog)
This work item was migrated to SorraAgents because all implementation code lives in this repo. Original tracking (comments, evidence, session history) lived on AH-0MVXVADEL005XNWM in the AI_Hell worklog and is preserved in the sections below.

## Problem

The plan skill's autoplan pre-check is meant to decide whether an item needs planning from its effort/risk. On this epic (8 planned children, multi-week scope) the pre-check reported:

- `effort: "Extra Small"`, `risk: "Low"` → `decision: "skip"`.

The zeroed estimate was written by the plan helper's own estimator call, not derived from the item:

```python
# skill/plan/plan_helpers.py :: run_effort_and_risk
payload = json.dumps({
    "issue_id": target_id,
    "o": 0, "m": 0, "p": 0,
    "certainty": 100,
    "assumptions": ["Auto-generated by autoplan decision"],
    "unknowns": [],
})
```

`orchestrate_estimate.py` faithfully aggregates that zero payload, so every autoplan run stamps:

- `effort: XS`, `risk: Low`, PERT `O=M=P=0.00h`, "No detailed WBS items provided".

Evidence: comment `AH-C0MVXV4TGO0066OWH` on AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 ("T-shirt size: Extra Small … Recommended (with overheads): 0.00h"), and the follow-on `# Auto-Plan Decision` comment `AH-C0MVXV4TVH003G62N` ("Decision: proceed to implement (effort and risk below threshold)").

## Impact

- `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` returns `skip` for **every** item, so the "small item" auto-skip path is indistinguishable from "the estimator wrote zeroes" — planning can be silently skipped for epics.
- The stored `effort`/`risk` fields are overwritten with false values, so the plan-approval gate (`Extra Large` + `High`/`Severe`) can never fire on real risk, and downstream scheduling reads a wrong estimate.
- Observed twice on this item: intake's autoplan pass and the plan session's pre-check both consumed the zeroed estimate.

## Expected behaviour

The autoplan estimate must not overwrite a work item's real effort/risk with a zero payload. Either:

1. derive the estimate from the item + its children (aggregate child WBS rows, count ACs/files), or
2. when no WBS/estimate inputs exist, leave `effort`/`risk` **unset** and return `decision: "error"`-equivalent "unknown" so the plan skill defaults to full planning (its documented conservative fallback), rather than writing `XS`/`Low`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` no longer posts `O=M=P=0` / `XS` / `Low` for an item that has children with non-trivial scope; a regression test covers an epic with children.
2. When the estimator has no real inputs, the work item's existing `effort`/`risk` are left unchanged and `plan-if-needed` falls back to full planning (or a documented `decision: "unknown"`), instead of `skip`.
3. A unit test asserts the pre-check returns `plan` for an epic whose children exist even if the estimator produces no numbers.
4. Existing plan_helpers tests still pass (full suite via the test skill).

## Key files

- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — `run_effort_and_risk`, `make_autoplan_decision`, `plan_if_needed`
- `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` — aggregation / zero-payload handling
- `skill/plan/tests/` — autoplan decision tests

## Related

- discovered-from:AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 (observed while planning the optimisation pass — AI_Hell worklog).
- Related (different root cause, already fixed): SA-0MSIUJQAK008AQV8 — only guards the *worklog-lookup-failure* path; the general zeroed-payload path remains.

## Plan (plan skill session, 2026-11-01)

**Implementation repo.** Every path in *Key files* above is relative to the
SorraAgents repo (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`); `skill/plan/` does not
exist in the AI_Hell checkout. The `AH-` item remains resolvable from SorraAgents
tooling through the shared prefix-to-sibling worklog scan
(`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py::_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`), so the fix can
be implemented in a SorraAgents worktree while tracking remains on this AI_Hell
work item.

**Reproduction observed during this session (2026-11-01T17:15Z).** Running the
pre-check against this very item reproduced the defect on itself:

- before the run the item's `effort` and `risk` fields were empty;
- `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed AH-0MVXVADEL005XNWM` returned
  `{"decision": "skip", "effort": "Extra Small", "risk": "Low"}`;
- the same run posted the zeroed `# Effort and Risk Report`
  (`O=0.00h, M=0.00h, P=0.00h`, "No detailed WBS items provided") and the
  `# Auto-Plan Decision` comment, and overwrote `effort`/`risk` with
  `Extra Small` / `Low`.

Those two bogus comments and fields are superseded by the genuine estimate posted
at the end of this planning session.

**Implementation sketch (test-first, one vertical slice).**

1. *Tests first* — `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py`:
   - epic-with-children case: an item with children and non-trivial scope must not
     yield `XS`/`Low`; `make_autoplan_decision` must not post the zeroed
     effort/risk report or the autoplan decision comment, and `plan-if-needed`
     must return `plan`.
   - no-real-inputs case: the item's existing `effort`/`risk` are left unchanged,
     no zero payload is written, and the decision is `plan` (never `skip`).
2. *Helper* — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`:
   - `run_effort_and_risk`: replace the hard-coded `o=m=p=0` / `certainty=100`
     payload with inputs derived from the item (children's stored effort/risk,
     child and AC counts), and return `None` instead of calling the orchestrator
     when no real inputs exist.
   - `make_autoplan_decision`: treat a `None` result as unknown → `do_plan=True`,
     write no `effort`/`risk`, and post no zeroed report/decision comment.
   - preserve `is_effort_risk_computed` idempotence: the unknown path must not
     write an `autoplan-decision-hash` comment, so a later run can still compute a
     genuine estimate.
3. *Defence in depth* — `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py`:
   only if needed, refuse or annotate an all-zero `o=m=p` payload rather than
   aggregating it into a confident `XS`/`Low`.
4. *Docs* — record the unknown-fallback in the plan skill pre-check section and in
   `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` (SorraAgents).
5. *Verification* — run the `skill/plan/tests` scope through the test skill, then
   manually re-run `plan-if-needed` against an item with empty `effort`/`risk` and
   confirm it returns `plan` and leaves the fields unchanged.

**Vertical slice.** No phasing is needed: the test, helper and doc changes ship as
a single end-to-end slice. No child work items were created.

**Note on AC 2 (clarification, not a rewrite).** The existing plan-skill decision
vocabulary is `skip` / `plan` / `error`; introducing a fourth `unknown` value
would break callers such as the autoplan dispatcher. AC 2 is therefore read as: the
*behaviour* is "unknown → full planning", expressed as `decision: "plan"`,
optionally with an explanatory `reason`/log line — the zero-write behaviour is the
observable "unknown" signal.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were asked in this session: the description's ACs and the
*Expected behaviour* section already resolve the issues that would otherwise have
needed an interview. The following are recorded as open questions/assumptions so the
implement session (and the Producer) can confirm them.

- **OPEN QUESTION (implementation repository) — directed to the Producer.** All
  *Key files* live in the SorraAgents repo, but this item is tracked in the AI_Hell
  worklog. *Assumption applied:* implement in a SorraAgents worktree and keep the
  work item here (prefix-to-sibling wl resolution makes `wl` work from either
  checkout). *Why it matters:* `implement.py start` selects the worktree from the
  repo it is invoked in, and `implement.py finish` refuses changes made outside that
  worktree — so the implement session must start in SorraAgents, not AI_Hell.
  *Alternative:* move/mirror this item into the SorraAgents worklog.
- **OPEN QUESTION (derive vs. unknown) — directed to the Producer.** AC 1 asks for
  no zero payload "for an item that has children with non-trivial scope"; AC 2
  allows an unset/unknown fallback. *Assumption applied:* derive from children's
  stored `effort`/`risk` when they exist, otherwise leave the fields unset and fall
  back to full planning. *Why it matters:* the derive path needs a defined
  aggregation rule (sum of child recommendations vs. max t-shirt vs. PERT).
  *Evidence:* `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` aggregates
  `items`/`o`/`m`/`p`; child items currently carry no WBS rows, so in practice
  most runs will take the unknown path until estimates are propagated.

Discovered while running `/skill:ship release` on 2026-11-02: the audit runner cannot
produce a persistable verdict for a subset of `in_review` items, so the release audit
gate can never pass for them. Two distinct defects compound.

discovered-from:AH-0MVZ6GSMY000VJMH (release-blocking recovery run)

## Defect 1 — Phase 2 / verdict re-ask fail with provider connection errors

Re-auditing these items fails identically on every attempt (4 attempts each on
2026-11-02, including serial runs with `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`):

- AH-0MVXWEDOH002LO1M
- AH-0MVXWEE3L004SPTC
- AH-0MVXWEEJM00813GK

```
Pi provider error: Connection error.
AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=3 parse_ok=0 parse_failed=0 timeouts=0
  child_skips=0 provider_errors=3 concurrency_waits=0 verdict_reasks=1 elapsed_seconds≈140
```

Phase 1 completes ("No code quality issues found"); **Phase 2 (deep analysis) and the
verdict re-ask both fail** and nothing is parsed. Observed error contexts in
`~/.audit_debug/AI_Hell/audit_debug_<id>.jsonl`: `{"context":"phase2_deep",
"reason":"provider_error"}` and `{"context":"verdict_reask","reason":"provider_error"}`.

**Not a provider outage:** in the same window a direct `pi -p "Reply with exactly: OK"`
returns `OK` immediately, and 20 other audits in the same pre-flight run succeeded. The
failing items' debug JSONL files are ~2 MB versus far smaller for the successes —
strongly suggesting an oversized request or an unbounded prompt/context is being sent
and the proxy drops the connection.

**Secondary observation:** the reported `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` (`elapsed_seconds`,
counts) is byte-identical across separate runs, which suggests the "Phase 2 skipped —
small, low-risk item" / script-failure path is replaying a cached summary rather than
reporting the current attempt. Worth verifying: a plausible reading is that a stale
abort-recovery state file short-circuits each retry.

## Defect 2 — verdict persistence rejects the assembled content

For the same items, `wl audit-show` stores a notice instead of a report:

> The audit pipeline completed, but the final persistence step rejected the assembled
> verdict content (malformed JSON / validation error). The full report could not be
> stored in the audit text field.

So even when Phase 1 produced a usable report, the verdict is unreadable by the gate,
and the item is permanently classified as needing a re-audit. The message says "A
re-audit may be required if the verdict data is needed in this field", but re-auditing
deterministically reproduces it (Defect 1).

## Impact

The audit gate (`check-audit-gate.js` / `check-final-validation.js`) treats these as
missing/stale audits, so remediation is attempted, fails, and the release blocks with
exit 6 and later exit 12 — with no path to green short of the runner being fixed. This
made the 2026-11-02 release impossible to complete.

## Environment

- `PI_PROVIDER=Local Proxy` (ContextHub `src/start.ts` proxy, 3-slot pool)
- audit runner: `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- concurrency during the run: another project (`SorraAgents`) was running
  `audit_runner.py issue --audit-children` concurrently, so saturation may contribute —
  but the failure reproduced serially with `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` and with no other
  AI_Hell audit running.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — For each of the three affected items, `audit_runner.py issue <id>` completes
  Phase 2 and records a parseable verdict (`parse_ok > 0`, `provider_errors == 0`);
  the raw provider-connection-error path is either fixed (e.g. bound the request size /
  chunk or truncate the payload) or fails with an actionable message naming the cause.
- AC2 — A completed audit's verdict is persisted and readable via `wl audit-show` for
  the affected items (no "persistence notice" instead of a report); a test covers the
  malformed-content rejection path.
- AC3 — `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` reflects the current attempt rather than replaying a

## Goal

Lock in the root cause of Defect 2 with a regression test that fails on today's
`persist_audit.py` and passes once persistence keeps the verdict header first.

**User story:** As the release producer, I want an audit that hit a subprocess failure to
still persist its verdict in the audit-text field, so a transient provider problem can never
hide a real verdict behind a persistence notice.

## Context / evidence (from the parent plan investigation)

- `skill/scripts/failure_notice.py` → `FailureNotice.wrap()` places the `====…` /
  `⚠ Script Execution Failure …` banner as the report's **first** line.
- `wl update --audit-text` accepts only a first non-empty line of exactly
  `Ready to close: Yes` or `Ready to close: No` (`inspectAuditFirstLine` in the worklog
  package, `src/audit.ts`); a banner-prefixed report fails with `audit-invalid-first-line`.
- `persist_audit._salvage_report_text` finds no broken JSON (`changed=False`), so the repair
  retry never runs and `_build_fallback_text` stores the misleading
  "malformed JSON / validation error" notice.

## Scope

- Add tests driving `persist_audit.persist_audit()` with an **injected runner** that emulates
  wl's real header validation (`--audit-text` whose first non-empty line is not a verdict
  header → rc≠0, stderr `audit-invalid-first-line`).
- Cover both rejection paths distinctly: (a) header/validation rejection of a failure-notice
  wrapped report; (b) genuine malformed-JSON content that the salvage pass can repair.
- No live `wl`, no network, no `pi` calls.

- AC1 — A new test fails on the current `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` (it asserts the
  report — not the notice — is submitted first) and passes once the fix child lands.
- AC2 — A test proves the genuine malformed-content path still salvages valid JSON prefixes
  and never fabricates verdicts (existing salvage contract preserved).
- AC3 — A test proves that when persistence fails for a non-JSON reason the notice names the
  real wl error and does not claim "malformed JSON".
- AC4 — `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/test_persist_audit_resilience.py` passes.

## Goal

Prove, with tests, that a run's `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` describes the current attempt and
that a leftover abort-recovery state file cannot short-circuit or distort a retry.

**User story:** As an operator debugging a failed audit, I want the reliability summary and the
failure evidence to belong to the attempt I just ran, so I am never misled by a previous run's
numbers or by stale recovery state.

## Context / evidence (from the parent plan investigation)

- `_rel_reset()` runs at the top of `cmd_issue` and the summary is emitted once per process, so
  the runner does not replay counters; the "byte-identical" observation is explained by the new
  report never being persisted (Defect 2), leaving the previous run's stored report visible.
- `audit_runner.py` only writes/removes `.audit_state_<id>.json`; it never reads it
  (`check-audit-gate.js` reads it after exit to restore status). A stale state file cannot
  short-circuit a retry today.

## Scope

- Tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_reliability_summary.py` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_abort_recovery.py`:
  (a) two sequential `cmd_issue`-equivalent runs with different outcomes produce *different*
  counters and summary values (no bleed-through between runs);
  (b) a pre-existing `.audit_state_<id>.json` (and a stale debug JSONL) present before a run has
  no effect on the verdict, the counters or the retry path, and is cleaned up as today;
  (c) the emitted summary reflects only calls made in this attempt (calls/parse_ok/
  provider_errors/timeouts/verdict_reasks).
- Assert the line remains greppable with the documented stable key order
  (`RELIABILITY_SUMMARY_KEYS` + `elapsed_seconds`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — Tests prove per-run isolation of the reliability counters and the emitted summary line.
- AC2 — A test proves a stale abort-recovery state file present before the run cannot change
  the verdict, counters or retry behaviour (documents current behaviour if no code change is
  needed).
- AC3 — The summary line keeps its stable key set/order and one-emission-per-run contract.
- AC4 — `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/test_audit_reliability_summary.py
  skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_abort_recovery.py` passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_reliability_summary.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_abort_recovery.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`

# Vitest failures are reported as `unparsed` infrastructure, never as structured test failures

## Problem

`run_tests.py` parses structured failures for every non-pytest command with
`parse_node_failures()` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`), which only
understands **Node TAP** output (`not ok <name>` lines). Vitest's default
reporter emits `FAIL |browser (chromium)| <path> > <test name>` plus a
`⎯⎯ Failed Tests N ⎯⎯` block, so a genuine vitest failure yields
`failures: []`.

Consequences observed live on `tce-main-street` (MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1,
2026-11-03):

- `implement.py finish` reported `reason: unparsed`, `notices:
  ["suite exited 1 with no parsable failures: all"]`, `failures: []`,
  `exit_code: 1` for a run whose stderr plainly contained
  `⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯ / FAIL |browser (chromium)| … / Error: Timed out
  waiting …`.
- The message therefore told the operator "infrastructure condition, not a
  code failure … the command or its configuration is the problem, not a
  test", which is wrong: two real browser test failures had occurred.
- The classifier's documented contract ("Structured failures always win: a
  genuine failure is never reported as infrastructure") is not met for
  vitest projects, which are the majority of the Node-side suites in this
  estate.
- The gate's facts (`configured_timeout`, `elapsed_seconds`,
  `slot_wait_seconds`, `exit_code`) were correct, so only the failure
  extraction is missing.

## Evidence

```
$ python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py finish MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1 --json
test_phase: {"reason": "unparsed", "failures": [],
             "notices": ["suite exited 1 with no parsable failures: all"],
             "configured_timeout": 3600, "elapsed_seconds": 427.8,
             "slot_wait_seconds": 0.0, "exit_code": 1}
command: npm --silent test && npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts && …
```

stderr (same run) contained:

```
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
 FAIL  |browser (chromium)| tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts > MainStreetScene browser tests > allows pressing Enter to end the turn when legal
Error: Timed out waiting for Turn Summary dialog after end-of-turn presentation after 40000ms (cap 16000ms)
 ❯ waitForCondition core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts:165:8
 ❯ tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts:657:4
```

## Desired change

- Add a vitest failure parser (default reporter `FAIL … > <test>` headers with
  the following `⎯⎯ Failed Tests` blocks, and the `junit`/`json` reporter as a
  fallback) selected when the resolved command runs vitest — the same way
  `parse_pytest_failures` is selected for pytest.
- Keep the fallback order: structured failure → classified infrastructure
  reason; a parsable vitest failure must never be reported as `unparsed`.
- Regression test: a fixture stderr containing a vitest `Failed Tests` block
  yields one structured failure, and the gate classifies it `test_failure`
  with a non-empty `failures` list.
- Also cover `npx vitest run --project browser <file>` command shapes, since
  the project label appears inside the FAIL header.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vitest failure block produces a structured failure record (test name, excerpt, stack trace), unit-tested against a captured fixture.
- `implement.py finish` classifies such a run as `test_failure` (not `unparsed`) with a non-empty `failures` list, proven by a gate-classification test.
- A genuinely unparsable non-zero run still falls back to `unparsed`/`killed` as today (no regression to the infrastructure vocabulary).
- Documentation (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) states which reporters are parsed.
- A failure carrying only the `❯ <file>:<line>:<col>` frame plus its source excerpt (the `FAIL … > <test>` header and `AssertionError:` line absent because the gate keeps only the last 1200 output characters) is still parsed into a structured failure whose failing location is that frame, so `reason` is `test_failure`.
- A non-zero vitest run with a `❯ <file>:<line>:<col>` frame is never classified `unparsed`/infrastructure: the frame is reported as the failing location even when no structured failure record can be built.
- A regression test pins the frame-only case using the captured excerpt from RISE-0MW5JFQCU001YYQK (README-diff tail + `❯ tests/the-rising/the-rising-docs.test.ts:2129:20`), asserting `test_failure` rather than `unparsed`.
- Captured-tail handling is verified so a `FAIL` header is not lost to trimming alone — either the failure block is captured whole (wider/anchor-based window) or the tail window is documented as sufficient because the frame parser no longer needs the header.

## Delta from RISE-0MW5JFQCU001YYQK (transferred 2026-11-06)

A second live occurrence — a `tce-the-rising` implement run
(`RISE-0MW4XICXH006AEVS`) — produced the same misclassification with a narrower
surviving output, so the vitest parser above must also handle the tail-trimmed
shape. The gate keeps only the last 1200 characters
(`implement.py::_tail_text`, `GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS`); the surviving tail was:

```
<README diff …>
 ❯ tests/the-rising/the-rising-docs.test.ts:2129:20
    2128|     expect(readme).toMatch(/rising-sweep-1000-progressivefaceoff-tie-n…
    2129|     expect(readme).toMatch(/not the parity target/);
       |                    ^
```

No `FAIL` header and no `AssertionError:` line survived, so a parser keyed only
on those lines would still report `unparsed`. The four delta acceptance
criteria above cover this.

Evidence: `/tmp/finish-RISE-0MW4XICXH006AEVS.log` (attempt 1,
`test_phase.reason = "unparsed"`, `failures: []`, `elapsed_seconds: 67.4`) and
`RISE-0MW5JFQCU001YYQK` (transferred here and closed as a duplicate on
2026-11-06).

## Related work

- `RISE-0MW5JFQCU001YYQK` (tce-the-rising) — second live occurrence; its unique delta (frame-only `❯` parsing, frame as the failing location, captured-excerpt regression and tail-window verification) was transferred to this item on 2026-11-06.
- `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — timeout/kill/unparsed classification and the deciding
  facts; this item closes the "genuine failure reported as infrastructure" gap
  in that contract.
- `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (tce-main-street) — validation run that surfaced it;
  red findings were triaged as `MS-0MW0M7TR0008GB1O` and `MS-0MW0M7UHT005CY6U`.

## Constraints

- Must not change the test command vocabulary or infrastructure classification
  for genuinely broken commands (e.g. ENOSPC, missing executables).
- Must work with both the `npx vitest run` shape and the `vitest run`
  direct-executable shape; wrapper commands (`npm test`) still fall back to
  marker detection.
- Must handle the gate's 1200-character output tail: the frame parser must
  work with truncated output where the `FAIL` header may be lost.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Vitest's default reporter output format is stable across
  versions. If a future Vitest release changes the `FAIL` header or
  `⎯⎯ Failed Tests` block format, the parser would need updating.
- **Assumption:** The 1200-character gate tail is sufficient to capture
  at least the `❯ file:line:col` frame for real failures.
- **Risk:** A very large test run with many failures could push the frame
  outside the 1200-char tail. Mitigation: the frame parser handles partial
  output independently of the FAIL header.
- **Risk:** The `❯ file:line:col` frame format might differ in other test
  runners. Mitigation: the frame parser is only invoked for vitest commands,
  and the regex is anchored to the Vitest frame style.

## Impact

Operators running browser tests with Vitest will see real test failures
reported as structured failures with the failing test name and excerpt,
instead of the misleading \"unparsed infrastructure\" message.
data.title: Vitest failures are parsed as unparsed infrastructure, not structured test failures

# Repeat `implement.py finish` (no diff) falls back to full scope and fails the gate on a staged inherited index

## Problem

When `implement.py finish` is re-run on a worktree whose change set is already committed and pushed (the documented recovery path after a failed push — *"Re-running `finish` on the retained worktree is idempotent"*), the changed-scope selection finds **no changed files** and falls back to **full scope** (`run_tests.py`: "changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope"). The full-scope run is gated by `implement.py`'s would-be-commit **temporary index** (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported for the suite). At least one test in the full suite (i.e. outside `skill/test/tests/`, which passes in the changed-scope gate) stages its own fixture paths into that inherited index, so `WouldBeCommitIndex.verify_unchanged()` reports:

```
gate evidence invalid: the temporary index changed while the suite ran
(tested tree edd255d9784e99f15aab25d143872678a8743eea, index now unreadable).
```

`finish` then enters the test-fix loop and, with no interactive stdin, aborts — so the work item never reaches `completed`/`in_review` even though its commit **is already pushed and green on `dev`**.

Observed 2026-11-03 on SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH (commit `7edd639cf`, already pushed; the repeat `finish` failed after 978 s).

## Why the existing guard did not name the offender

`conftest.py`'s autouse `_inherited_index_unchanged` fixture exists exactly for this (SA-0MVWQ4FZ4003S0GE), but it compares **staged trees**: when the inherited index becomes *unreadable* (`git write-tree` fails — the observed case, e.g. a fixture staging paths that do not exist in the live worktree), `IndexWatch.poll()` has nothing to report, so no test is named. `finish` only reports the anonymous end-of-suite verdict.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Offender identified and fixed.** The test(s) that honour an inherited `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and stage into it instead of their own repository's index are found (full-scope run: root `tests/` and every `skill/*/tests/` dir whose conftest does not drop `GIT_INDEX_FILE` — `skill/shared/tests`, `skill/audit/tests`, `skill/ship/tests`, `skill/standup/tests`, … have no such conftest) and made hermetic (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` / `run_git()`). A full-scope run under an exported `GIT_INDEX_FILE` must leave that index byte-identical.
2. **The guard reports an unreadable index too.** `IndexWatch.poll()` (and/or the autouse fixture) must treat "the inherited index can no longer be read/written" as a violation and name the offending test, not return silently — otherwise the same failure stays anonymous.
3. **Repeat `finish` reaches the terminal status.** Re-running `implement.py finish <id>` on an already-pushed, clean worktree persists `completed`/`in_review` (the no-op-push path of OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58). Regression test: a repeat finish (no diff, already pushed) both succeeds and leaves the item terminal.
4. **No cost regression.** A repeat finish of a fully-committed, already-pushed item must not require a *fresh* full-suite execution when a green full-scope entry already exists for that tree/state (today the fallback uses a **tree-kind** fingerprint that the *worktree-kind* dev-push entry cannot satisfy, so it re-runs ~16 min). Either reuse the pushed-commit's clean-state entry or document the cost explicitly.
5. All related documentation updated (implement reference: repeat-finish semantics and the full-scope fallback) and the full project test suite green.

## Key files (predicted)

- `conftest.py`, `skill/shared/inherited_index_guard.py` — unreadable-index reporting.
- Suspect offenders: `skill/shared/tests/test_resolve_repo_root.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_temp_index.py`, and other `skill/*/tests/` files invoking raw `git` without `fixture_git_env()`.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — repeat-finish path / full-scope fallback cost.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.

## Evidence

- `finish` log (this item's origin): "WARNING: Implement run_tests: changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope." then the `gate evidence invalid … index now unreadable` notice; suite elapsed 978 s; the item's commit `7edd639cf` was already on `origin/dev` with a green `scope: full` worktree-kind cache entry (`git_state 07f6b8d8…`, 5854 passed / 14 skipped).
data.title: Repeat implement.py finish falls back to full scope and fails the gate on a staged inherited index

Discovered-from: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO (during F2 SA-0MVPI400Y001FOM1 completion).

## Problem
When `implement.py finish` falls back to full-scope testing it runs the suite with a temporary index exported as `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. A pre-existing test fixture stages into that inherited index instead of its own repository index, so the finish gate reports:

```
reason=infrastructure
gate evidence invalid: the temporary index changed while the suite ran (tested tree ..., index now unreadable). A test staged into the inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE instead of its own repository's index; the verdict cannot be attributed to the would-be-commit tree. Fixture git commands must use a hermetic environment (for example shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()).
```

Observed while finalising SA-0MVPI400Y001FOM1: the commit was already on origin/dev and the dev pre-push gate was green, but a redundant finish re-run failed after ~904s on the full-suite fallback (changed-scope was unavailable because the tip was already on dev).

## Expected
The offending fixture should scrub `GIT_INDEX_FILE` via `shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` (or equivalent) so the finish gate can attribute the tested tree. Identify the test named by the guard's report when run under an inherited index.

## Impact
Not blocking (the authoritative dev pre-push gate runs in-place, not with a temp index). It affects redundant finish re-runs and any finish that falls back to full scope.

# Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in SorraAgents

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (0)

_None — only hooks below are pending._

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite, worklog-post-pull

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

Created from the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA. Pi session `herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004`, log `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-11-04T07-55-10-163Z_herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004.jsonl`.

# Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf `finish` fail after the work has landed

## Problem statement

On 2026-11-04 a single leaf session implementing two items (`WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R`,
`WL-0MW1VITA8009RLHQ` in ContextHub) spent far more time fighting git than
writing code. Five independent failures compounded, and the worst of them leaves
an item that **cannot be completed through the workflow at all**.

| # | Symptom | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transient SSH auth failure is not classified as retryable → hard failure | blocking |
| 2 | Non-fast-forward is detected but a leaf session gets no automatic rebase-and-retry | blocking |
| 3 | `finish` cannot converge when the commit **already** landed on `origin/dev` | blocking |
| 4 | The push gate re-runs the full canonical suite on every retry attempt | cost |
| 5 | A full-suite gate failure under concurrent load is indistinguishable from a real regression at the point of failure | diagnosis |

### Evidence

**1. Flaky SSH auth (~1 in 3 attempts).** Measured directly, seconds apart, from
the same shell with no credential change:

```
try1: 75f64a61...  refs/heads/dev     (OK)
try2: git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey).
try3: 75f64a61...  refs/heads/dev     (OK)
```

`ssh -T git@github.com` also alternated between authenticated and
`Permission denied (publickey)`. There is no `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` in these sessions
(they run over SSH with an on-disk `id_ed25519`), so each connection is a fresh
key handshake — which is where the flakiness lives. Separately GitHub returned a
non-auth transport error once:

```
! [remote rejected]   HEAD -> dev (Internal Server Error)
```

`_push_to_dev` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) classifies only
non-fast-forward (`non-fast-forward` / `fetch first` / `remote contains work`).
Everything else — including `Permission denied (publickey)` and
`Could not read from remote repository` — falls through to
`LOG.error(...); return False`, i.e. an unconditional hard failure with a
misleading "Commit is local and can be pushed manually" hint.

**2. No rebase-and-retry for a leaf session.** `PushNonFastForwardError` carries a
`rebase_cmd` for the caller, and `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` includes
`("local_dev_fast_forward", ...)` / `("main_checkout_lock", "lock_held")` — but
that retry budget is applied by `phase_drive` to **driven children**. A plain
leaf `finish` invocation fails outright. Observed: `origin/dev` advanced **three
times** during one item's lifecycle (concurrent runs pushed
`WL-0MW109HU60042BVW`, `WL-0MW109IIN009PADE`), and every one of those required an
operator-side fetch/rebase/push loop.

**3. `finish` cannot converge once the commit has landed.** For
`WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R` the push eventually succeeded, and
`git merge-base --is-ancestor 58834b09 origin/dev` confirmed it was on the remote
(and `git log origin/dev` showed it). Re-running `finish` to complete the
lifecycle then *failed again* — it re-attempts the push, hits the flaky auth, and
on failure resets the item to `status=open` with `assignee` cleared:

```
INFO: Restored status=open for WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R (failure exit, assignee cleared)
WARNING: Push failed. Commit 58834b09 on branch ... is local and can be pushed manually.
```

The workflow therefore had no path to `in_review`; the lifecycle had to be
completed by hand with `wl update --status completed --stage in_review`, after
independently verifying ancestry. That manual step is the automation failing
open, not a design.

**4. Full-suite suite re-run per attempt.** Every push attempt runs the
pre-push gate (`push gate: running the full canonical suite (--scope full
--strict-git-env)`, ~180–260 s). Eight failed attempts ≈ 30+ minutes of pure
gate overhead. With `--no-cache` runs for diagnosis on top, the same tree was
fully tested at least four times in one session.

**5. Load-induced gate flake reads as a code failure.** One push attempt ended:

```
ERROR: Full test suite failed - the push to dev/main is blocked.
```

Re-running the identical tree: `327 passed | 1 skipped; 4580 passed | 5 skipped`
— green. The failures were seven unrelated files failing to *load*
(`Cannot find package '@worklog/shared/worklog-paths'`, i.e. a missing shared
build) under heavy concurrent load from sibling agent runs. Nothing in the
operator-facing failure said "load/environment", so the honest reading was "my
change broke the suite".

## Goal

A leaf `finish` run in a busy multi-agent checkout completes the item through
the normal lifecycle when its work is valid, treating transient git transport
and ref-race failures as recoverable, and never leaves an item stranded in
`open` while its commit sits on `origin/dev`.

User stories:

- "As an agent running `finish` on a repo where several sessions push in the same
  minute, I want a transient transport or non-fast-forward failure retried
  automatically, so a ref race does not cost me the work item's lifecycle."
- "As an operator, I want `finish` to tell me plainly whether the push failed or
  whether the push landed and a *verification* step failed, so I know whether to
  retry, rebase, or investigate."
- "As an agent whose push already landed, I want re-running `finish` to reach
  `in_review` without re-pushing, so the workflow can always be completed."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Transient transport failures are classified and retried.** Auth/transport
   signatures (`Permission denied (publickey)`, `Could not read from remote
   repository`, `Connection reset`/`timed out`, `Internal Server Error` on the
   remote side) are classified as **infrastructure**, distinct from a real
   content rejection. Retried on a bounded budget with backoff (reusing the
   existing `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT` semantics), and surfaced as such in the
   report — never as a bare "push failed".
2. **Non-fast-forward is retried for leaf runs, not only driven children.**
   `finish` rebases onto `origin/dev` and re-attempts within the same bounded
   budget. A rebase conflict is a genuine stop with an actionable message (never
   forced/mutated silently).
3. **`finish` converges when the commit already landed.** If `HEAD` is an
   ancestor of `origin/dev` (verified against the remote, not a stale
   remote-tracking ref), `finish` treats the push as satisfied, skips the
   re-push, and proceeds to the terminal `completed`/`in_review` transition
   instead of resetting the item to `open`.
4. **Push-failed and verification-failed are distinguishable** in both the log
   and the work-item comment: `push_failed` (nothing landed) vs
   `push_landed_but_unverified` (pushed, ancestry/gate assertion failed) vs
   `already_pushed`.
5. **No status regression on an already-landed push.** An item whose commit is on
   `origin/dev` is never returned to `open` by a transport failure.
6. **Reduced gate cost per attempt.** At most one full-suite gate run per
   `finish` invocation even across internal retries (the gate result for an
   unchanged tree is reused, or the retry path is reachable only *after* a
   successful gate), so N transport retries do not mean N full suites.
7. **A load/environment gate failure is labelled as such.** When the gate fails
   with suite *load* errors and a retry passes on the identical tree, the report
   says "infrastructure/load flake (suite failed to load on attempt N, passed
   unmodified on attempt N+1)" rather than reporting a code failure. This must
   not weaken the gate: a reproducible failure still blocks the push.
8. **Regression tests** drive a fake remote/git shim through: transient auth
   failure then success; non-fast-forward then successful rebase; ref race where
   the commit already landed; rebase conflict stop; and the labelled load-flake
   case.
9. **Documentation** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md` "When `finish` refuses" and the
   dev-push gate section) reflects the retry taxonomy and the three push
   outcomes.
10. **Full project test suite passes** (`/skill:test`).

## Plan

1. Extract push-outcome classification (transient vs content vs already-landed)
   from `_push_to_dev` into a pure, testable helper; unit-test the signature
   table. → verify: new test file green, table-driven over the five observed
   messages.
2. Add the bounded infrastructure retry + rebase-and-retry to the leaf `finish`
   path (reuse `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS`/`DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT` rather than a
   second mechanism). → verify: shim-driven tests for each recovery path.
3. Add the already-landed short-circuit (remote-verified ancestry) before the
   push, and guarantee no `open` regression in that case. → verify: test that a
   finish over an already-pushed commit reaches `in_review` with zero push
   attempts.
4. De-duplicate gate execution across internal retries. → verify: assertion on
   the shim's invocation count.
5. Label load-flake gate failures; keep reproducible failures blocking.
   → verify: paired tests (same tree fails-then-passes = flake label; fails
   twice = blocked).
6. Update `SKILL.md` and record the taxonomy. → verify: docs review, then
   `/skill:test` full.

## Key files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_push_to_dev`, `PushNonFastForwardError`,
  `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS`, `phase_finish`, the main-checkout lock guard, the
  termination/finish report.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — "When `finish` refuses", dev-push gate.
- Tests: the implement skill's existing python suites (fake-remote/shim fixtures).

## Risks & notes

- **Do not weaken the gate.** Retrying a *content* rejection or a reproducible
  suite failure must remain a hard stop. Only classified-transient conditions
  and labelled load flakes are retried, and a retry must re-verify the tree.
- **Never force-push.** Rebase-and-retry only; a conflict stops with an
  actionable message.
- **Remote-verified ancestry** is mandatory for the already-landed short-circuit:
  a stale `origin/dev` remote-tracking ref would otherwise let an unpushed commit
  be treated as landed. Fetch (or `ls-remote`) before asserting.
- **`main-checkout.lock` is working as designed** and is out of scope: it
  correctly fail-closed when a concurrent run held it, and a leaf session
  waiting on a live holder is safer than racing it. The gap is only that a leaf
  run has no bounded wait — consider that separately (the drive path already has
  `_wait_for_main_checkout_lock`).
- **Environment note (not a repo defect):** these sessions run over SSH with no
  `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, so every connection is a fresh key handshake. A per-session
  ssh-agent or `ControlMaster` would remove the transport flake at the source;
  that is an operator-environment remedy, and the work item's ACs deliberately do
  not depend on it being adopted.
- **Observability.** Record the retry taxonomy and the three push outcomes on the
  work item comment, so a post-hoc reader can tell a transport flake from a real
  rejection without re-running anything.

## Related

- Discovered during the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA follow-up, while
  implementing `WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R` (commit `58834b09`) and
  `WL-0MW1VITA8009RLHQ` (commit `f5566e2d`) in ContextHub.
- ContextHub `WL-0MVHP5S01006GDDV` — repo pre-push hook does not run the test
  suite (canonical gate unenforced at push): the counterpart that made the gate
  mandatory, and therefore made these retry costs visible.
- The `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` / `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT` machinery
  (LP-0MVWEP292000ODBS) is the existing precedent this item extends to leaf runs.
- `WL-0MW109HU60042BVW`, `WL-0MW109IIN009PADE` — the concurrent ContextHub runs
  whose pushes advanced `origin/dev` mid-flight.
data.title: Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf finish fail after the work has landed

# Harden /tmp inode headroom — age-based cleanup for test churn directories (host runbook)

## Goal (user story)

As the host owner of a multi-agent workstation, I want age-based cleanup of the
directories that test and build runs churn in `/tmp`, so inode headroom is
reclaimed automatically and a future runner that skips the framework prune
still cannot exhaust `/tmp` inodes.

## Context

Follow-up to the critical framework item (disk-backed `TMPDIR` + stale
pytest-root prune in `run_tests.py`/`implement.py`). That fix prevents new
inode pressure from the test runner; this item is the **host-level belt-and-
braces**: `systemd-tmpfiles` currently only carries `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d`,
so rapid multi-agent churn (stale `pytest-of-*` roots, Playwright/Chromium
profiles, `tsx`/node compile caches) can still fill the tmpfs inode table long
before the 10-day sweep. Observed in practice: `/tmp` at 100 % inodes
(1,048,576 total) while byte usage was ~24 %.

## Desired change (option 3)

Add age-based cleanup rules (systemd-tmpfiles preferred; cron acceptable where
tmpfiles is unavailable) for the high-churn temp directories, with an age
threshold longer than the longest test run, and document a runbook so the
remediation is repeatable.

Candidate patterns (refine during implementation):

- `/tmp/pytest-of-%u/pytest-*`
- `/tmp/playwright*`, `/tmp/.org.chromium.Chromium.*`, `/tmp/.com.google.Chrome.*`
- `/tmp/tsx-*`, `/tmp/node-compile-cache*`

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Rules installed and version-controlled/documented.** Age-based cleanup
   rules exist for the churn patterns above (e.g. `/etc/tmpfiles.d/pi-test-tmp.conf`
   with `e`/`q` lines, age ≥ 1 day), with the exact content recorded in the
   repo (runbook or a committed template under `docs/dev/` or `scripts/`).
2. **Verified.** `systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run` (or the cron equivalent)
   lists the intended removals, and a before/after `df -i /tmp` demonstrates
   reclaimed inodes. Evidence captured in a work-item comment.
3. **Safety.** The age threshold is strictly greater than the longest full-suite
   run (currently ~48 min measured worst case), rules are user-scoped where
   possible, and the active `pytest-current` target / newest root is never
   removed.
4. **Runbook.** `docs/dev/testing.md` (or a new `docs/dev/host-hygiene.md`)
   documents install, verify, rollback, and the inode-exhaustion failure
   signature (`ENOSPC` in Playwright `createContext`, `df -i /tmp` at 100 %,
   gate `reason: unparsed`/`infrastructure`).
5. **No repo code change required for the cleanup itself** beyond the committed
   rule template/runbook; if a scripted installer is added, it is idempotent
   and requires explicit root/host opt-in.

## Key files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/testing.md` or `docs/dev/host-hygiene.md` — runbook + rule template.
- Optional: a committed `scripts/` template for `/etc/tmpfiles.d/` (documented,
  not auto-installed without opt-in).

## Constraints

- **Requires host/root access** (`/etc/tmpfiles.d/`, `systemd-tmpfiles`). The
  repository change is documentation/template only; the host change is applied
  by the operator and evidenced in a work-item comment.
- Do **not** add rules that delete recent or active test roots.
- Complements, and does not replace, the framework TMPDIR + prune item.

## Related work

- Critical framework fix (option 1 + 2): disk-backed `TMPDIR` + stale
  pytest-root prune in `run_tests.py`/`implement.py`.
- Observed during **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** (tce-main-street) dev-push gate.

## Risks

- Over-aggressive age thresholds can delete a long-running test's temp files —
  mitigate with a threshold well above the measured worst case and user scoping.
- Host config drift between machines — the committed rule template keeps it
  reproducible.
data.title: Harden /tmp inode headroom — age-based cleanup for test churn directories (host runbook)

# finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase, and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly

## Goal (user story)

As an agent whose `dev` push follows a concurrent `dev` advance, when `implement.py finish`
cannot fast-forward the main checkout before the push, I want finish to still leave the main
checkout's `dev` at the pushed commit after the recovery rebase, and to report a
pushed-commit-guard refusal distinguishably (pushed sha, gate HEAD, gate tree) naming the
worktree push as recovery — instead of a generic push failure.

## Background

Cross-reference: **LP-0MVWB6AOH001MAB0** (llm worklog) — "finish pushes from the main checkout
after a refused local-dev fast-forward, so the pre-push pushed-commit guard refuses". The
producer decided (2026-11-05) that the residual scope lands here (SorraAgents) and the llm item
is kept as a cross-reference that owns no code.

The core symptom (push from the main checkout) was already fixed by **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3**:
`phase_finish` Step 6 and `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` now push from the worktree that holds
the commit. The residual gaps are:

- **AC1 (fast-forward retry).** `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` is called only once, in Step 5,
  *before* the push. When it is refused with `local_dev_diverged` / `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`
  because a sibling moved `dev`, the recovery rebase produces a commit that *is* based on
  `origin/dev`, but the fast-forward is never retried, so the main checkout's local `dev` stays
  behind the pushed commit.
- **AC4 (distinguishable guard refusal).** When `.githooks/pre-push` §3a refuses a push because
  the gate tree is not the pushed commit (or is dirty at it), `git_push_to_dev` finds no
  `gate_reason=` line and reports a generic push failure. Finish cannot tell the operator that
  the guard refused, nor surface the pushed sha / gate HEAD / gate tree the guard printed.

## Scope

In scope: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (the fast-forward retry inside the non-fast-forward
recovery, and a distinct pushed-commit-guard-refusal classification) and its regression tests.

Out of scope: changing `.githooks/pre-push` in consuming projects. The guard's existing stable
diagnostic text is the contract this item detects against; a hook-side `gate_reason=` emission is
a separate follow-up owned by the llm item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After a **refused** local-dev fast-forward (`local_dev_diverged` / `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`),
   when `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` rebases the feature branch onto `origin/dev`, `finish`
   **retries** the fast-forward for the rebased commit and records the retry in
   `report["steps"]["local_dev_fast_forward"]`. When the retry succeeds, the main checkout's
   checked-out `dev` HEAD equals the pushed commit before the retry push.
2. The retried fast-forward never fails the finish: a second refusal is recorded (with its
   reason) and the push still proceeds from the worktree — the current recovery behaviour is
   preserved.
3. `finish` detects the pre-push pushed-commit guard's refusal from its stable diagnostic text and
   reports it distinguishably as `report["steps"]["push"]["reason"] == "refused_by_pushed_commit_guard"`
   carrying the **pushed sha**, the **gate HEAD** and the **gate tree** parsed from the guard's
   output, with recovery guidance that names the worktree push. A non-guard push failure keeps its
   existing classification (`test_failure`, `timeout`, `subject_mismatch`, …).
4. Regression tests drive the **concurrent-move shape** (worktree based on `dev~1`, another commit
   landed on `origin/dev`) and assert the guard's preconditions hold at push time: pushed sha ==
   gate-tree HEAD and the gate tree is clean; and assert the main checkout's `dev` is advanced to
   the pushed commit after the recovery rebase. A second test asserts a guard-refusal stderr is
   classified `refused_by_pushed_commit_guard` with the three values, and a generic failure is not.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Guard: `.githooks/pre-push` §3a (LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9); its refusal prints
  `ERROR: pre-push gate refuses this push: the tree it would measure is not the pushed commit.`
  followed by `pushed commit  (refs/heads/dev): <sha>`, `checked-out HEAD: <sha>`,
  `gate tree: <path>` (and a dirty-tree variant).
- `git_push_to_dev` is around line 4815; `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` around line 10021;
  `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` around line 6783.
- Related completed: SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3 (push from worktree), SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI (gate reason
  vocabulary / transport retry).
data.title: finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` returns the **candidate ref name** (`origin/dev`) rather than the SHA resolved by `git merge-base`, and `compute_changed_files()` then runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` against that name.

When an implement worktree's branch base is *behind* the ref (a stale base — e.g. the branch was forked while local `dev` lagged `origin/dev`), diffing against the ref includes **dev-side** commits that are not part of the change set. `select_group_from_changed_files()` then picks test groups for unrelated work.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ (ContextHub store) — the stale-base session in which this was observed.

## Evidence

- Observed on 2026-11-05 in a ContextHub implement session (WL-0MW3JIYIR002RCP8): a docs + `tests/setup-tests.ts` change set ran `npm test -- packages/herdr/src` because the stale base made the diff include dev-side `packages/herdr` commits.
- Current code (`run_tests.py`, `_resolve_merge_base`, ~line 506): the loop runs `git merge-base <candidate> HEAD`, then `return candidate` (the ref name) — the resolved `proc.stdout.strip()` SHA is discarded.
- `compute_changed_files()` (~line 462) passes the returned value straight into `git diff --name-only <base>`.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — depend on correct changed-file selection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on changed-scope runs exercising the code that actually changed.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when my worktree forked from a base behind `origin/dev`, I want changed-scope selection to measure only *my* diff, so the gate runs the right tests.
- As an operator, I want a stale base to degrade into a smaller diff, never into an unrelated named group.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_merge_base()` returns the SHA resolved by `git merge-base` (falling back to the next candidate only when `merge-base` yields nothing), never a bare ref name.
- [ ] `compute_changed_files()` diffs against a merge-base SHA, so commits that exist on the ref but not on the branch base are excluded from the change set.
- [ ] Regression test: a fixture repo whose branch base is one commit behind the target ref — the changed-file set must contain only the branch's own files, not the ref-side files.
- [ ] Fallback behaviour preserved: with no usable base the function still returns `None` and callers fall back to full scope (no crash).
- [ ] Documentation updated where the changed-scope base semantics are described (`skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`) if the returned value's contract changes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Probe/read-only of git state; no new runtime dependencies; reuse existing helpers (`_git_inspection_env`, `run_cmd`).
- Behaviour change must be conservative: an unresolved base must still fall back to full scope rather than an empty diff.
- Related but distinct from SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66 (unqualified `origin/dev` ref *ambiguity* with a shadowing local branch) — both live in the same function, so either item may be implemented first; if both are taken together, keep the two fixes as separate commits.
- All written output in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_resolve_merge_base()` must return the merge-base SHA; `compute_changed_files()` consumes it unchanged.
- `skill/test/tests/` (or the existing test-skill test location) — regression test for a stale-base fixture.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document the returned-value contract if it is described there.

## Related work

- ContextHub `WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ` — Main-checkout local dev diverged from origin/dev (the stale-base incident; records this hand-off).
- `SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66` — Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous (adjacent defect in the same function).

data.description:
## Headline

Make the audit skill immune to a dirty/stale main checkout by running its
execution-dependent work (full-suite green-run gate, and ideally the whole
Phase 1/2 pipeline) inside a **fresh detached worktree checked out at the
latest `origin/dev`** (or the item's merged tip), so an un-pushed in-flight
commit sitting on the main `dev` branch can never contaminate an audit.

## Problem statement

`audit_runner.py` resolves ALL git-derived audit content (HEAD sha,
file-scope manifest, changed files, repo index, working-tree hash, green-run
attestation, and the F3 full-suite execution cwd) against the **local
checkout at the launch cwd** (`TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT`). The merge gate
(`_integrate_into_dev`, SA-0MT456M27001LRTL) and the stale-audit-base guard
(`_audit_base_freshness`, SA-0MT9EK1UU000DT1R) both integrate/verify against
`origin/dev`, but the pipeline still EXECUTES against the launch checkout.

Observed failure (2026-11-06, audit of RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH in
tce-the-rising): the main checkout's `dev` branch carried a **local-only,
un-pushed, in-flight commit** (`d538e51`, RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K) that
modified `risingMatchHarness.ts`/`src/TheRisingAdversary.ts`, and was 6
commits *behind* `origin/dev`. The F3 full-suite gate ran `npm test` in that
contaminated checkout, failed on four integration suites (all import the
changed harness), and produced `Ready to close: No` with AC8 partial on an
item whose own scope was green at its tip. The merge gate passed because the
item's commits ARE ancestors of `origin/dev`; the stale-base guard passed
because they are also ancestors of the local HEAD — neither checks that
local HEAD == `origin/dev` or that there are no extra un-pushed commits.

The stale-audit-base guard only flags "delivered on origin/dev, absent from
local HEAD" (behind). It does not flag **ahead-with-extra-commits** (in-flight
work parked on the main checkout) or **aside** (local HEAD not an ancestor of
origin/dev), and it does not move execution into an isolated worktree.

## Users

- **Audit consumers (producers, implement agents)** — want an audit verdict
  that reflects the state of merged, checked-in dev — never a developer's
  un-pushed local experiments parked on the main checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit runner resolves a **fresh, detached worktree at the latest
   `origin/dev`** (fetched before worktree creation) as the execution base
   for the full-suite green-run gate (F3) — the suite runs from that
   worktree, never from the launch checkout — and the worktree is removed
   afterward.
2. The stale-audit-base guard is extended to also abort (with the same loud
   remediation message) when the launch checkout is **ahead of /
   divergent from** `origin/dev` (local HEAD contains commits not in
   `origin/dev`), since an audit must never run against un-pushed in-flight
   work; a launch from a clean worktree of the owning repo stays valid.
3. Where feasible without changing verdict semantics, Phase 1/2 file-scope
   content (manifest, changed-file list, repo index, working-tree hash) also
   resolves against the origin/dev worktree rather than the launch checkout,
   so evidence never reflects a stale/dirty tree.
4. AC1–AC3 are covered by tests using a local bare "remote" with a dirty
   local checkout ahead of origin/dev (an un-pushed commit touching a
   harness file) — asserting the audit refuses/isolates rather than emitting
   misleading `partial`/`No` verdicts.
5. Existing behaviour is unchanged for a clean launch (launch checkout at
   origin/dev, worktree launches, `--do-not-persist`, batch/issue modes,
   `--no-execute`, child in-main-slot screens).
6. Documentation: audit skill reference (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`)
   and the audit SKILL.md are updated to state that audits execute inside a
   fresh origin/dev worktree and never against a stale/dirty launch checkout.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — base resolution for F3 suite
  execution, file-scope manifest, and the stale-audit-base guard.
- `skill/audit/scripts/test_cache.py` — cache keys are cwd-scoped; executing
  in a worktree changes the cwd used for cache hits.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — existing runner unit tests (fresh-base + guard
  coverage to extend).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — docs.

## Related work

- `RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH` (tce-the-rising) — the audit that exposed this
  gap (spurious AC8 partial from a dirty launch checkout).
- `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` (tce-the-rising) — the work item whose un-pushed
  commit contaminated the main checkout.
- SA-0MT9EK1UU000DT1R — the existing stale-audit-base guard (behind-only).

## Out of scope

- Enforcing "no commits on the main checkout" (that is implement-skill
  hygiene, tracked elsewhere); this item only makes the audit robust to it.
- Changing the merge gate's integration semantics (that is already
  worktree-isolated at origin/dev).
- Verdict semantics, prompts, or the freshness/content-fingerprint gates.

## Implementation constraints (from audit review addenda)

Recorded from the `herdr-audit` review comments on this item
(SA-C0MW50DKU2005VDO1, SA-C0MW50KPXB001WENO), written after the
RISE-0MW12YSRB007979Y and RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH incidents. These constrain
AC1/AC2/AC4 — they add no new scope.

- **Ordering (AC2 vs F3).** The ahead/divergent check must be evaluated early
  in `_phase_gate`, right after owning-root resolution and *before*
  `_auto_green_run_outcome`, and/or F3 must be fully isolated on the
  origin/dev worktree (recommended: both — isolation first, early abort as
  belt-and-braces). Otherwise the contaminated suite runs and the triage
  helper auto-creates a spurious critical `test-failure` child parented to
  the audited item before any guard fires.
- **Guard scope.** Abort only when the launch checkout *is the owning repo's
  main checkout* and its `dev` is ahead/divergent. A feature-worktree launch
  (`<owning>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*`) legitimately has a HEAD ahead of
  `origin/dev`; the existing behind-only check suffices there (AC5).
- **Toolchain in the execution worktree.** Reuse the merge-gate integrator's
  `node_modules` symlink convention (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) and add submodule
  initialisation — mirror `implement.py::_ensure_submodules`
  (`git submodule update --init --recursive`, SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ). In
  tce-the-rising `core/` is a gitlink submodule and an empty one makes every
  suite command fail at startup (`vitest failed to load config`). Init
  submodules *before* symlinking `node_modules`
  (ordering hazard: SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ).
- **Cache expectations.** The main checkout's `.worklog/cache` and the
  worktree git-dir `test-cache` are distinct, so an isolated F3 run starts
  with an empty cache and re-executes fresh at the clean base — expected, not
  a regression (see also SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L, cache-key identity).
- **Test fixture.** The AC4 bare-remote fixture must include a tracked
  submodule and an absent `node_modules` so the toolchain-initialisation step
  is pinned by a test.
data.title: Audit skill: always run the suite/pipeline in a fresh worktree at latest origin/dev

discovered-from: WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG (ContextHub)

## Observed

While driving the ContextHub epic WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG (5 children) with `implement.py drive` (headless transport), the first driven child (WL-0MW55V82X009JYRV) hit a red changed-scope gate caused by a pre-existing, environment-only test failure (a hyphenated `TMPDIR`, tracked separately as WL-0MW5C6XS00071DWN). Instead of stopping after triage, the child:

1. created a brand-new work item (WL-0MW5C6XS00071DWN) and ran `implement.py start` for it;
2. edited files inside that item's worktree — the child had been spawned with `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` and `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH=<its own worktree>`, yet it `cd`-ed into a sibling worktree and edited there (the worktree-placement guard did not fire because the sibling worktree is a legitimate linked worktree);
3. added a dependency edge from its own item onto the newly created one;
4. ran repeated full suites (`--scope full --force`) for ~20 minutes, triaging unrelated performance-test failures.

The driver was stopped by the operator, the spurious edge removed, and the epic finished serially by hand. No data was lost; one commit that the child produced in the sibling worktree was later completed properly.

## Why it matters

A driven child that writes outside its own worktree can race the session that owns that worktree, silently widen the epic's scope, and consume the host's test slots. The existing placement guard only detects 'work landed in the main checkout', not 'work landed in a *different* linked worktree'.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child refuses (or is refused) any write whose path resolves into a linked worktree other than `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`, with an actionable message naming both roots.
- A child whose `finish` gate is red because of a failure it did not introduce reports and stops (triage → work item), instead of starting that work item's implementation itself.
- Regression test: a simulated driven child that `cd`s into a sibling worktree is detected and the run fails closed (no status mutation of either item).
data.title: implement.py drive: a driven child strays into another work item's worktree when its first finish gate is red
